Sports.title: Jamie Carragher talks up two Liverpool transfers who could follow Andoni Iraola
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher talks up two Liverpool transfers who could follow Andoni Iraola

Liverpool hired Andoni Iraola in the summer off the back of his impressive work at Bournemouth, with the new Reds boss tipped to possibly raid his former club

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher has talked up some potential transfer targets for Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

Jamie Carragher has suggested that Liverpool could go after Alex Scott or Rayan given their previous history with Andoni Iraola.

‌



The Reds are in the midst of their new era under the Spaniard, who moved to Anfield off the back of three impressive years with the Cherries. Iraola's final season saw him lead Bournemouth into Europe for the first time, with Scott and Rayan among his top performers.

‌



Bournemouth have sold their top players annually for huge profits - last season they offloaded Antoine Semenyo and prior to that had let Milos Kerkez head to Liverpool.

‌



The Cherries dug their heels in over the summer and were determined to keep Scott despite links with Chelsea and Manchester United. Rayan, who was named in Brazil's World Cup squad, is another Carragher has hailed as he suggested Iraola may use his links to bring them to Merseyside.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



He said of Scott on Sky Sports: "I think he’s a wonderful player. There was a lot of interest in him in the summer and because Liverpool have a former Bournemouth manager, you almost think: will there be a link or will there be a couple of players moving that way?

"I thought Rayan was fantastic last season as well. It will have been really good for him to get a goal in midweek because he probably hasn’t been himself at the start of the season. There are some fantastic players here at Bournemouth."

Kerkez was among the players to shine at the Vitality Stadium under Iraola, which prompted Liverpool to go after him. However the full-back has struggled at Anfield with his new boss looking to unlock the form he showed so regularly two seasons ago.

‌



View 2 Images Alex Scott and Rayan are two of Bournemouth's leading lights

Scott could prove to be a target come the summer with Liverpool's midfield copping criticism this term. Iraola has the likes of Dominik Szoboszlai, Ryan Gravenberch and Alexis Mac Allister to choose from, whilst Florian Wirtz has been deployed centrally as the team's No 10.

A move for Rayan is less likely given the recent investment in the team's frontline. Bradley Barcola recently became Liverpool's third £100m plus signing over the last two summers, joining Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz. Cody Gakpo, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz are also forward options for Iraola.

Article continues below

Liverpool were victorious at the Vitality on Sunday afternoon, beating Bournemouth 1-0 thanks to a strike from Alexander Isak.

Sports.title: Manager holds back tears on live TV as he's told about tragic death of his friend
Sports.content:
Manager holds back tears on live TV as he's told about tragic death of his friend

German football legends Peter Hermann died on Saturday and Niko Kovac was told of the death of his friend live on television following Borussia Dortmund's win over Stuttgart

View 2 Images Niko Kovac was clearly upset after being told about the death of a friend (Image: Sky Sports Germany)

Borussia Dortmund manager Niko Kovac was left distraught after he was informed of the death of his friend and colleague during a post-match interview on Sky Sports. Peter Hermann, Kovac's assistant at Bayern Munich, died following a battle with neurodegenerative illness, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), aged 74.

‌



Dortmund came away victors against Stuttgart, thanks to Maximillian Beier's goal, to continue their perfect record at the top of the Bundesliga. But Kovac was unable to hold onto the joy of another three points as the news of Hermann's passing broke while he was on the air on Saturday.

‌



Presenter Sebastian Hellmann received the news during an interview with Kovac and informed the Dortmund boss, in addition to pundits Lothar Matthaus and Julia Simic. Kovac was visibly upset by the news and said: “It leaves me a little short of breath.

‌



“One or two months ago I was still trying to speak to him, that was no longer possible at all. Unfortunately, his illness was incurable.

“I am deeply saddened, a good person has left us.”

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



While Kovac went on to cancel a media appearance with ZDF’s Aktuelles Sportstudio on Saturday evening. "We had actually planned to speak with BVB coach Niko Kovac at this point," explained presenter Katrin Müller-Hohenstein.

"However, he canceled at short notice because he had just learned of the death of his long-time colleague and assistant coach Peter Hermann,"

Kovac cut an emotional figure during his press conference. The Croatian had to fight back tears as he spoke about his friends death.

‌



View 2 Images Niko Kovac worked with Peter Hermann at Bayern Munich (Image: TF-Images/Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

“From me and also from my brother, our sincere condolences to Peter’s family," he said. “A great man has left us.

‌



“Not only as an assistant coach in Munich, but also as assistant coach when I was still a player in Leverkusen. Really a shock.”

Herman was a veteran of more than 1,000 matches as an assistant coach. The German spent time with Dortmund, Bayern Munich, FC Nuremberg, Schalke 04, Hamburg SV, Bayer Leverkusen and the Germany national team as he played a pivotal role at the highest level of German football.

Leverkusen paid tribute to their former coach with a glowing endorsement. "More renowned and respected in the sport than many a head coach," their tribute read.

‌



"An undisputed football expert, Hermann never made a fuss about himself. Down-to-earth, modest, loyal. A man with a great sense of humour and without a trace of vanity. A team player, a meticulous worker and a good listener."

Bayern were similarly effusive in the regard they hold Hermann. "Arm in arm with Franck Ribéry, deep in conversation with David Alaba, beer showers with Arjen Robben – there are countless scenes that have stayed in the memory and show what an extraordinary figure Bayern lost on Saturday," they said.

"Peter Hermann, the indispensable right-hand man of treble-winning boss Jupp Heynckes, passed away at the age of 74, and German football is mourning the loss of a unique bridge between generations, a man of great humanity and a true specialist in his field."

Sports.title: Middlesex beat Leicestershire to end 36-year List A trophy wait
Sports.content:
Middlesex ended a 36-year List A trophy drought by beating Leicestershire Foxes by 31 runs to win the Metro Bank One Day Cup in a low-scoring final at Trent Bridge.

Ryan Higgins made a superb maiden List A hundred from 115 balls with Harry Duke (55) backing him up as their 135-run sixth-wicket partnership steered Middlesex from 71-5 to 231 all out after Foxes all-rounder Ian Holland took 5-36 and wicketkeeper Ben Cox held five catches. Higgins and Duke were making their first appearances for Middlesex in this year's competition.

New Zealand international batter Nick Kelly hit an equally brilliant 103 (107 balls) to lead a Leicestershire fightback from 79-5 but it was not enough to haul his side over the line, Tom Helm (3-32) claiming his vital wicket in a superb late spell as the Foxes were bowled out for 200.

In an impressive performance in the field by Middlesex, Toby Roland-Jones (3-27) showed his quality and 21-year-old pace prospect Naayva Sharma (3-37) finished as the competition's leading wicket-taker with 20.

Against a background of turmoil off the field, the win is a first for Middlesex in a List A final since they beat Derbyshire to lift the 1990 Refuge Assurance Cup.

Leicestershire, still reeling from the points deduction in the Rothesay County Championship that makes relegation almost certain, had hoped to ease the pain winning a second Metro Bank trophy in the space of four seasons but it was not to be.

Put in, Middlesex were 32-3 in the 11th over and five down in the 22nd - all snared by the immaculate Cox.

Image: Middlesex's players celebrate winning the Metro Bank One Day Cup

Nathan Fernandes slashed at one from Holland, who dismissed Max Holden in similar fashion, and Tom Scriven found a thin edge to remove skipper Ben Geddes for a duck.

Josh De Caires fell victim to a superb leg-side grab before Luke Hollman nicked a first-ball googly from Rehan Ahmed and Cox celebrated again.

But Duke - on loan from Yorkshire as cover for the injured Joe Cracknell - provided the support Higgins needed before a top edge to extra cover brought his undoing, Helm was leg before to Rehan and Higgins perished one ball after going to his maiden List A hundred, failing to clear long-on, looking for a 10th boundary.

Image: Middlesex wicketkeeper Harry Duke played a crucial innings

The Leicestershire innings almost exactly mirrored that of Middlesex as they slipped to 32-3 and 79-5.



Sharma dismissed Foxes captain and former Middlesex batter Stephen Eskinazi, caught at second slip, and Hamza Shaikh leg before, veteran Roland-Jones having Rishi Patel caught at deep square leg.

Roland-Jones claimed two more victims in Ahmed, leg before, and Cox, caught behind.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player New England Test coach Stephen Fleming has outlined what he wants from his players going forward

Leicestershire found themselves needing someone to step up as Higgins had and Kelly answered the call. Allowing few scoring opportunities to pass him by, reaching 50 from 52 balls with six fours and a pick-up for six off Sharma as he and Holland added 50 for the sixth wicket.

Ben Green's departure added more pressure, with 57 still needed. Kelly, who twice hammered Zafar down the ground for more sixes, kept the Foxes in the hunt, reaching 100 from 103 balls.

But, after needing treatment for cramp, he pulled Helm straight to deep square. Ajaz Patel fell to a stunning catch at backward point by Zafar off Helm, before Scriven was the last man to go, caught at mid-off.

Sports.title: Smith thrashes Price to win World Series after Littler's shock exit
Sports.content:
Ross Smith thrashed Gerwyn Price 11-5 to become World Series of Darts Finals champion, while Luke Littler's hopes of a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 were dashed in the quarter-finals.

Smith won the last six legs, fired in 11 maximums, recorded back-to-back ton-plus finishes and went at 46 per cent on his doubles as he overwhelmed Price in Amsterdam on Sunday night to claim his second PDC major, after the 2022 European Championship.

Price, who missed a host of doubles in the back end of the match as his checkout percentage dropped to 26, has seven PDC majors in total, including three Grand Slams and the 2021 World Championship, but none since the World Series Finals in 2022.

Speaking bluntly afterwards on ITV4, the Welshman said: "I am playing some good darts, I am earning some good money. If I never win a major again I really don't care as long as I am doing well.

"I am gutted I've lost but if I never win another major then I have a good family, I have invested all my money. I really don't mind. I will be gutted for half an hour but on Tuesday I'll be in Tenerife.

"I was absolute rubbish in that final but don't take anything away from Ross. He was brilliant and took his opportunities."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Littler's bid for a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 is over after defeat to Jonny Clayton at the World Series of Darts Finals

Smith stars in Amsterdam as Littler crashes out

While Smith celebrates his fifth trophy of the season - this triumph in the Netherlands follows the Hungarian Darts Open and International Darts Open on the European Tour and a couple of Players Championship events - Littler is processing a shock defeat.

Having won the first five majors of the year - as well as the World Cup of Darts for England alongside compatriot Luke Humphries - Littler was hoping to claim all 11, only to be trounced 10-4 by Jonny Clayton in the quarter-finals.

Smith overcame Josh Rock in the last eight before dumping out remaining home hope Gian van Veen in the last four, while Price surged towards the end of matches to eliminate James Wade and Clayton before being floored by Smith.

Image: Smith can now celebrate his second PDC major title

Smith said: "It feels a bit mad, to be fair! I am absolutely made up with the win. I am so happy. [Price] is one of the best in the world, so to beat him you have to up your game.

"I always say in my interviews that I take each game as it comes. I play one game at a time. They are all finals and I give it my all. That is working for me at the moment."

Sports.title: Hits and misses: Maresca's Man City serve up pure chaos as Gakpo shines
Sports.content:
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Manchester City and Sunderland

Man City's captivating but chaotic 5-3 win over Sunderland could not have been further removed from the picture of control so often associated with City under Pep Guardiola. "We want to control but the other team don't want to allow us," Enzo Maresca reflected.

Sunderland made command of the game very difficult, but City equally did themselves no favours.

Maresca had warned of the size of the task pre-match - and so it proved. "I knew how good they are, off the ball very aggressive," he added, after the Black Cats terrorised the Etihad. Rarely have City conceded so much territory or given up so many chances at home, nor do they often ship three goals.

Why were they so open?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brian Brobbey scores for Sunderland at Man City

Brian Brobbey served up another masterclass in hold-up play, just as he did against Arsenal last week. Except on this occasion he matched his physical presence with three excellent goals. Every time Brobbey won his duel against Ruben Dias - which was often - there was space to play off.

He was joined in waves of attack by Enzo Le Fee, before Nilson Angulo and Thomas Meunier swiftly arrived from wide. Suddenly City were overloaded. And it happened time after time. Neither Elliot Anderson nor Enzo Fernandez could get to grips with the physical battle, unable to cope when Sunderland pressed man to man or played longer.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brobbey completes his hat-trick in a losing cause for Sunderland

City were out-duelled by a substantial amount, outrun too. Brobbey won 10 of the 12 duels he contested and drew a game-high five fouls. He could not be shackled, a clear winner of the tug-of-war.

But fortunately for Maresca, City were able to play Sunderland at their own game for enough of the match to score five times themselves. They picked on mistakes, digging deep to get the job done the anti-Pep way. Imperfect but effective.

Perhaps that should count for something, too.

Laura Hunter

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Fulham and Manchester United.

Michael Carrick is getting a reputation for the way he calmly bats away criticism of his Man Utd team, contrasting with the noise of those detractors. He has had to do that more and more in the past week, with a Manchester derby loss followed by a Carabao Cup collapse, and now a scrambled point at previously bottom-club Fulham.



At Craven Cottage he was asked about United's joint-worst start to a Premier League season and pointed to fine margins. The 25-yard stunner at Everton, the incorrectly awarded City goal, the bizarre own goal at Fulham and two strikes against posts earlier in the game. He has a point.

But the problem is the accumulation of poor performances is starting to add up. As Carrick would say, it's not been all bad in any game but the positives are being outweighed by United's shortcomings. Physically, defensively, and in possession United have been found wanting in key moments and keep paying the price.

A 10-point gap has already yawned open to table-topping City and the prospect of United improving on last season's third place seems unrealistic right now.



"It's still a big season ahead," Carrick defiantly told the press on Sunday evening. But a big shift, encompassing more than just finer details in a game, is required if it's to be a successful one.

Peter Smith

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Bournemouth and Liverpool

In every single Liverpool game he has started this season, Cody Gakpo has produced a golden moment in front of goal.

A goal at Newcastle on the opening weekend, a silky assist against Nottingham Forest, assists for both goals in the win over Ipswich, another one and a goal against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup - but this intervention in the 1-0 win at Bournemouth was the best of the lot.

With Liverpool struggling for attacking influence, Gakpo's hard-fought run and cross down the right wing was vital in the build-up to Alexader Isak's winner. "The difficult part of the goal is from him," said Iraola about Gakpo, who is unfortunate not to be accredited with the assist.

Image: Alexander Isak celebrates with Cody Gakpo

But Gakpo also starred defensively at Bournemouth, winning more duels than any other player on the pitch. He shut down one of the Cherries' biggest threats. "I know Adrien Truffert very well and he demands a lot from you defensively. Cody has been very important in both ways," added Iraola.

When Gakpo is absent, Liverpool are not the same team - as seen in the goalless draw with Fulham where the Dutchman was only fit enough for the bench.

Looking at this form, it is absolutely staggering that Liverpool considered sanctioning the sale of Gakpo this summer. Where would they be without him?

Sam Blitz

From the highs of their first win in Europe against Real Sociedad on Thursday to the lows of yet another defeat in the Premier League.

Bournemouth now go into the three-week international break without a win. A sour note to leave on given the joy that followed from their victory in San Sebastian.

Neither side impressed at the Vitality Stadium and for the most part, the Cherries looked the more likely team to go on and snatch three points.

But with Justin Kluivert sidelined through injury and no other changes made from the team in midweek, they just did not have the legs to go one step further in front of goal.

Marco Rose has made just two changes to their Premier League starting XIs this season, the fewest of any side.

That is not sustainable while balancing European football. Rotation is needed to keep this squad fit; otherwise they risk slipping into an unwanted relegation battle this season.

Patrick Rowe

Alvaro Arbeloa says Fulham are improving and it is a fair assessment after draws against Liverpool and Man Utd at the end of a testing start in the Premier League.

A third consecutive defeat in early September at home to Crystal Palace heightened concerns Fulham may be in a relegation fight after four trouble-free seasons under Marco Silva, but they have something to build on heading into the international break.

Josh King has been their brightest player across the first five games with two goals and is showing why he is so highly regarded by the club having come through the academy. David Affengruber, an £8.5m summer signing from Elche, shone on debut at centre-back against Liverpool and appears to have dislodged Joachim Andersen for now.

Gonzalo Garcia scored on the opening day of the season following his move from Real Madrid but has managed just two shots on target from 15 so far.

The next six weeks will be pivotal for Arbeloa. He has more time to work with his squad now ahead of fixtures against the three newly-promoted clubs when the season resumes.

David Richardson

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Leeds United and Crystal Palace

Crystal Palace arrived at Elland Road with 11 goals conceded from their opening four Premier League games. They left with a clean sheet and, on balance in the second half, will probably feel they could have taken all three points.

This was a spirited, disciplined performance from Palace. They came out after the break with a completely different mindset and put Leeds under pressure.

Leeds were strangely flat. Dominic Calvert-Lewin was starved of service for long periods and even when the chances did arrive, Palace goalkeeper Walter Benitez was there to deny him.

In the end, 0-0 felt like a reflection of two sides who cancelled each other out, but Palace can take far more encouragement from this performance than Leeds can.

For Pierre Sage, though, this is the sort of defensive display he will hope can become the foundation of a turnaround.

William Bitibiri

Sports.title: 'I deserve to be in!' - Spaun uses Team USA snub as fuel for Wentworth win
Sports.content:
JJ Spaun said he played with a "huge chip on his shoulder" during his BMW PGA Championship win and used being snubbed by Team USA's Presidents Cup side as motivation for his Wentworth victory.

Spaun became the first player since Byeong Hun An in 2015 to win the DP World Tour's flagship event on debut, posting a final-round 67 to claim a two-shot success over Rory McIlroy, Aaron Rai, Adam Scott and Manuel Elvira.

Last year's US Open champion also won on the PGA Tour earlier this season at the Valero Texas Open and finished 10th in the Presidents Cup qualification standings, having also made his Team USA debut in the Ryder Cup last September.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Spaun reflected on his debut win at the BMW PGA Championship and how the 'stars aligned' for him

Spaun was controversially overlooked for a captain's pick by Brandt Snedeker in his line-up to face the International Team in the biennial contest, live from Thursday on Sky Sports, with the 36-year-old pleased to respond by claiming a statement victory.

"The stars aligned this week for me to come out on top," Spaun said. "I'm just grateful to have the opportunity and play well and give myself a chance and came out with a W.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Manuel Elvira handed Spaun victory after a nightmare double-bogey on the final hole at Wentworth

"We [him and Snedeker] haven't spoken. I played with a huge chip on my shoulder. I definitely had something to prove this week, but everything happens for a reason. I'm so delighted to be here and just to even play this event.

"The extra motivation, I think that is the willpower that you have. Being left off the Presidents Cup team a couple weeks ago was very disappointing and I wanted to prove that I deserve to be on that team.

"I took care of my business this week, so all the best to the team next week at Medinah - I'll be watching from my couch!"

Sports.title: Neville: Carrick must stop defending Man Utd players after Fulham 'disgrace'
Sports.content:
Gary Neville has urged Michael Carrick to stop defending Manchester United players after another troubling performance in their draw at Fulham.

While on Sky Sports co-commentary, Neville described their start to the second half at Craven Cottage as "the worst 15 minutes I have ever seen Manchester United play".

In that time, Carrick's side conceded a horror own goal from Lisandro Martinez, before Matheus Cunha's late deflected strike avoided a third straight league defeat.

The 1-1 draw followed losses to Manchester City last Sunday and a capitulation in the Carabao Cup third round against Brighton while there was a lack of urgency and energy at times from Man Utd in west London although Carrick dismissed the idea that his side were "passive".

Neville said: "I've never seen a Man Utd team walk out of possession as much as that. Michael has just said there was nothing wrong with the team's energy.

"Michael has got to stop defending them. I get why he's defending them; he's loyal, he wants his players to work for him, and obviously there's a long way to go in the season.

Image: Manchester United's numbers out of possession

"Both teams were the same. I called them mannequins. I've never seen a United team walk around as much as that. No alertness, no aliveness. No 'on your toes'. You should always be on your toes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville was unhappy with the lack of running from the Manchester United team out of possession during their draw with Fulham in the Premier League.

"Always shifting up two or three yards. They were just walking when Fulham were in possession. Fulham had 46 passes in the first couple of minutes to get their first shot.

"I don't know how many over-10-pass sequences Fulham had in that game, but the international break has come at a great time. There needs to be a rebalance.

"Very rarely do I say a team doesn't work hard or is lacking in effort. That's the ultimate criticism you can give a group of players.

"I'm always very careful to say that, but in those first 15 minutes of that second half, Man Utd and generally for the first 60 minutes, were a genuine disgrace. Nowhere near good enough without the ball.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Fulham and Manchester United.

"Michael is of course saying something different to us than he is saying privately. That would've really worried me. People will ask questions about him, but he knew that when he took the job.

"But there's no panic in that sense - no one is putting pressure on Carrick - but if those types of performances continue, he will find himself in a lot of trouble. They've got to work harder than that for him."

A joint-worst start to a Premier League season for Man Utd Manchester United have won just five points from five league games this season – their joint-fewest at this stage of a Premier League campaign (also 5 in 2014-15).

Neville also elaborated on how United's personnel is causing Carrick a headache. He said: "I wish he could play all of those attacking players, but they are going to kill him defensively.

"It's not just the defence and the back four that are causing him a problem - Mbeumo and Rashford are too high and wide. They don't narrow back in. You've got Tielmans and Mainoo in midfield who are a little bit one-paced. Baleba will probably come in there. Bruno floats around a little bit, and then Cunha floats around a little bit.

"You've got these five or six players who are better with the ball than without the ball.

"It would be great to see them score loads of goals and maybe concede one or two and go and win games, but there is going to have to be a reset from the point of view of defensive structure because there are far too many of them walking on the pitch."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fulham boss Álvaro Arbeloa said there were key decisions that didn't go his side's way, and felt that the referee 'didn't like' to let Manchester United lose.

Cunha: They put in more energy than us - we cannot accept this

Cunha also said Man Utd lacked energy at Craven Cottage, telling Sky Sports: "It is frustrating for us. After the goal, we played much better and had a lot of character. It needs to be from the start. It is only one point but we should never play for one point.

"It is hard. They put in more energy than us, we cannot accept this. We need to do our best. We need to improve in every single position. It is only the beginning. Last season was the same, with noise around, but we finished third."

However, Carrick did not subscribe to the same view, adding to Sky Sports: "I didn't think we did [look passive]. Did you think we were passive? Football is a difficult game.

"We controlled a lot of the first half and we played a lot of good football today. There is going to be spells when you don't have it go your own way.

"The goal they scored, and arguably there is a foul at one point on Matheus [Cunha], and it is two deflections. It goes their way. To expect total dominance for the whole game, I don't think anyone gets that in this league."

Sports.title: Ireland blow 19-point lead to lose to USA in WXV Global Series
Sports.content:
Freda Tafuna of the United States starred against Ireland

Ireland blew a 19-point lead to suffer a 40-36 loss to the USA in their opening game of the WXV Global Series.

The hosts romped to a 17-0 lead in the first 20 minutes in Dublin, with Vicky Elmes Kinlan opening the scoring and Dannah O'Brien scoring a conversion.

Tries from Cliodhna Moloney-MacDonald and Aoife Wafer made it 24-12 at half-time.

Early in the second half Ireland extended their advantage to 19 points, leading 31-12.

But the visitors, led by a player-of-the-match performance from Freda Tafuna, patiently clawed their way back into the clash with four successive tries from Kathryn Treder, twice, Hallie Taufoou and Tafuna.

Tafuna's try, scored while Kinlan was in the sin-bin, set the tone for the USA's first win over Ireland since 2018.

Scott Bemand's side are back in action next weekend away to Japan on Sunday at the Dexcom Stadium.

Sports.title: 'Might be time to wrap it up' - O'Neill to consider Celtic future
Sports.content:
Martin O'Neill will take stock as his future as Celtic boss comes under further scrutiny following the 1-0 defeat by Rangers at Parkhead.

The Light Blues cruised to a 3-0 League Cup win over the Hoops at Ibrox last Sunday and, in the Scottish Premiership rematch, a first-half strike by Ryan Naderi took Derek McInnes' side to within two points of the Hoops at the top of the table going into the international break.

In his second spell as permanent manager after two stints as interim boss last season, O'Neill was under growing pressure going into the game after the 3-1 loss to Ferencvaros at Parkhead on Thursday night.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ryan Naderi fired Rangers to victory at Celtic Park

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Rangers.

Following another poor performance, the 74-year-old spoke about entering a period of self-reflection.

"I genuinely will reflect and see," the Northern Irishman said. "It's a matter of whether I can help the team. The manager is supposed to be able to do that. I will look at that this week.

"I think every single time something crops up and things don't go so well, age plays a part. And, do you know what, they might be right. I'll be 110 in two years' time so it might be time to wrap it up.

"I will reflect on the games and speak to the board. You never know, they may well want to speak to me. I'll try to get a couple of days away and see how it goes."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player O'Neill felt the latest Old Firm defeat was a close game but he was shut down by former striker Chris Sutton who was left disappointed by the loss

Asked what would happen if he reflected, then decided he could not improve the team, O'Neill replied: "By that time, I will promise you, I'll let you know.

"I don't know. I'll have a look."

O'Neill addressed the growing negativity within the Hoops support, saying: "Well, I think they're absolutely entitled.

"I mentioned this to you on Friday, absolutely entitled to, of course.

"And I'm not immune from criticism. Far from it. Absolutely and utterly far from it.

"I think there's every reason to ask, 'can you turn this round? Can you change the whole thing?'

"We are, as I said, two points clear, so I have to kind of look at the bigger picture at this minute.

"But I knew that we were in a big, big fight anyway, with both ourselves, Rangers, and Hearts again, who are far from out of anything.

"It's a long season ahead. It's not the first time I've been questioned about my managerial time. So, yeah, I'll have a look at it. I will reflect and see."

'Celtic have big problems'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kris Boyd and Neil Lennon on Celtic's dismal display against Rangers

Former Celtic manager Neil Lennon on Sky Sports:

"He's [Martin O'Neill] changed formation, he made four changes midweek. He's trying to find a recipe to get some fluidity.

"Rangers were the far superior team, not just in physical attributes and running power, but football.

"They played all the football. Celtic were a lot better than they have been in the first half, without being brilliant.

"But second half, totally disjointed, totally outplayed. Outworked, which is the worst thing you can label at a team. Really disjointed, battered, actually battered.

"All the best players were in a blue shirt today. Celtic have a lot to ponder and a lot to work out.

"They've got an international break, which is probably coming at a good time for them. I know a lot of them may be away playing for their countries but there needs to be a total reset because the last three performances in the space of a week have been very poor."

Sky Sports' Chris Sutton:

"Knowing Martin, he'll be greatly concerned. I don't like to disagree with him but it wasn't a close game. There was a massive gulf between the teams.

"I can't actually remember a Celtic team getting such a doing at Celtic Park from a Rangers team, which happened today.

"It looked like Celtic were making it up as they went along. Rangers were better in every department.

"Celtic have got big problems. They were smashed by Rangers and that's a concern."

Sports.title: Heath bounces back after blowing lead to win first LET event
Sports.content:
England's Charlotte Heath secured her maiden Ladies European Tour title in dramatic fashion, holding off a host of challengers to claim victory at the La Sella Open in Denia, Alicante.

The 24-year-old rookie started the final round with a four-shot advantage and, despite seeing her lead disappear during a tense Sunday afternoon, she held her composure to card a final-round 73 and finish at 10 under par, two shots clear of the field.

After three weather-affected days, gusting winds continued to add an extra layer of difficulty, and set the stage for a thrilling finale at one of the LET's premier events.

Heath's front nine featured a solitary bogey at the fifth as she turned in 37, while Germany's Helen Briem mounted a strong challenge and briefly drew level at nine under par through 13 holes. However, Briem immediately dropped a shot at the next, allowing Heath to reclaim the outright lead.

As Briem and Shannon Tan of Singapore slipped back on the closing stretch, Italy's Alessandra Fanali posted the clubhouse target at eight under par.

The strongest challenge ultimately came from Englishwoman Alice Hewson, who surged into contention with a birdie finish. Standing over an eagle putt on the 18th that would have tied the lead, Hewson narrowly missed before tapping in for birdie, joining Fanali at eight under par.

Image: Heath bounced back after losing a four-shot lead before going on to win by two strokes

Heath was left needing a composed finish to seal the biggest victory of her career.

On the final hole, Heath split the fairway with her drive before finding a difficult position to the right of the green with her second shot. Unfazed, she pitched to nine feet and confidently rolled in a birdie putt to cap a remarkable week, ending her week with two birdies and two bogeys across the back nine.

The victory earns Heath her first LET title, a £128,722 (€150,000) winner's cheque and an unforgettable breakthrough moment in her rookie season.

"It's incredible," said Heath. "This year, I've gone out in the leading group twice before, so I guess it's third-time lucky.

"It was incredible having Alex [Long] on the bag. He kept me so calm and just reminded me that I'd played good golf all week. When the pressure is on, negative thoughts can creep in, so I'm very, very happy to get it done."

Heath admitted the mental challenge was as demanding as any shot she faced.

"You probably didn't want to be in my head on that golf course today," she said. "I was thinking I was going to shank it, hook it, pull it. You never know. Alex kept the ship steady all day."

Hewson, meanwhile, reflected on another strong performance at a venue she has long enjoyed.

Image: England's Alice Hewson finished tied for second at eight under par

"It's been a really solid week," she said. "I played some nice golf out there and probably didn't hole as many putts as I would have liked.

"La Sella is always one of my favourite stops on tour and having my whole family here made it even more special."

What's coming up next?

The LET travels to Italy for the Buccellati Ladies Italian Open at Golf Club Milano, which will be played from September 25-27.

Sports.title: Carrick disputes Cunha’s claim that Manchester United lacked energy in Fulham draw
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick rejected the suggestion that his Manchester United players lacked physical fitness after they snatched a last-gasp 1-1 draw at Fulham on Sunday. The statistics showed the home side ran a collective 6.6km more than United, whose goalscorer in the 89th minute – Matheus Cunha – was critical of his team’s efforts.

United were poor after the restart at 0-0, leading up to a disastrous Lisandro Martínez own goal in the 63rd minute, with Cunha saying they had to give more. “In the beginning of the second half, Fulham put in more energy than us and we cannot accept this,” Cunha said.

The draw was not the result Carrick or United wanted after a week during which they lost the derby against Manchester City and exited the Carabao Cup against Brighton; both matches were at Old Trafford. Carrick will take it under the circum­stances and he tried to ­highlight the positives which he said took in the never-say-die spirit of his ­players. They fought until the end and were rewarded when ­Cunha’s shot from distance took a heavy deflection off the ­Fulham defender David ­Affengruber to wrongfoot Bernd Leno.

Carrick said he did not agree with Cunha’s comment about the collective energy levels. “I don’t, ­particularly,” the manager said. “The way we finished the game … it didn’t look like that for me. I was quite happy with the way we finished the game. We kept pushing. I don’t think that’s an issue, no.

“The response [to the own goal] was really pleasing … the way we went about trying to get back into the game. [We] kept the ideas, kept the patience, kept the real purpose to it. We finished on a positive, which is a small step for us … without ­getting carried away it’s a good step. We came to take three points but at least we’ve taken something to build on ­moving forward.

“It has been pretty fine ­margins [so far this season] that have flipped it [the wrong way]. I know we can do better, we need to do better at certain things. But I’m not despondent and down because we’re showing some good signs.”

A section of the United support booed Carrick’s decision to ­withdraw Kobbie Mainoo in the 80th minute; the manager sent on Mason Mount in his place. “There’s always going to be ­certain reactions when you’re ­making changes,” Carrick said. “I ­understand. We’re chasing the game and ­everyone’s a little bit emotional. I don’t take any negatives or offence to it.”

Carrick was asked whether he felt a certain deflation among the fans, who have been expecting a big season from United. “It’s still a big season ahead,” he said. “It’s a long season and you’re going to have spells through it. That’s part of the journey.

“I’m not playing it down. We wanted more points. I’m not saying everything’s great. I understand the frustration. But deflation is certainly not what we have within the club. The players didn’t have that on the pitch today and that’s what will carry us through the season.”

The Fulham manager, Álvaro Arbeloa, was unhappy with the officials and he claimed they did not want United to lose after what had ­happened in the City game last ­Sunday when Erling Haaland’s ­winner was allowed to stand despite his teammate, Enzo Fernández, being in an offside position.

Quick Guide Neville says United 'absolutely pathetic' Show Gary Neville branded Manchester United’s early second-half display against Fulham as the worst he had seen in more than 45 years. Reflecting on United’s lethargic, error-strewn start to the half, the Sky co-commentator called the period “absolutely pathetic”, saying: “I’ve watched Manchester United since the age of five and that’s the worst 15 minutes I’ve ever seen. I’ve never seen such a lack of effort. What must Michael Carrick be thinking?” Guardian sport Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Arbeloa highlighted what he said was a soft free-kick in Harry ­Maguire’s favour on halfway, which came 35 seconds before Cunha’s equaliser. Maguire felt the contact from the ­Fulham substitute, César Palacios.

“All the fouls for them,” Arbeloa said to Sky Sports straight after the game. “You can see before they scored, the foul against Maguire … he’s a guy who is 100 kilos. Every decision was for them. And I knew. I knew after the game against Manchester City that they [would not] let Manchester United lose here.”

Arbeloa rowed back on his comments in his main press conference but still said he was “not really happy”. The referee, Peter Bankes, gave Fulham the benefit of the doubt in the 86th minute when a Martínez shot hit Calvin Bassey’s hand inside the area. Bassey did put his hand up but it remained close to his body.

Sports.title: Maresca dismisses title talk as ‘too early’ after Manchester City take over at the top
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca dismissed ­Manchester City pulling ahead in the title race after Sunday’s 5-3 win over Sunderland, with the manager stating it is “too early” in the season.

The frantic victory at the Etihad Stadium gave City 15 points from their opening five league matches, three more than Arsenal after the champions lost at Brighton on Saturday. Maresca was asked about his team being top before the three-week international break.

“It’s much better to win games,” he said. “In this moment, it’s better to have three points more than less, no doubt. But at the same time, we know that it’s quite early. The international break is good. We can review what we have done and what we can do better, and at the same time, we can relax a little more.”

Of the victory against Sunderland, Maresca said: “I prefer to win 1-0 than 5-3 but I expected a very difficult game – I knew how good they are, off the ball, very aggressive. I knew it was a difficult game but happy because we found a way to win the game.

“We scored five. We could have scored probably more goals. So that means that we create enough, but at the same time we need to avoid conceding goals like today. We had four clean sheets in a row and today we conceded three goals.”

City twice took the lead in the first half after goals from Enzo Fernández and Rayan Cherki, yet each time Sunderland found equalisers from Brian Brobbey, before Antoine Semenyo’s 43rd-minute strike gave the home team a 3-2 half-time lead.

After the break the winger’s second made it 4-2 before Brobbey completed his hat-trick to make it 4-3 on 59 minutes. While Erling Haaland’s late strike completed the scoring Brobbey became the first player to score three and be on the losing side in the Premier League since Roque Santa Cruz in Blackburn’s 5-3 loss at Wigan in December 2007.

At 3-2 Elliot Anderson appeared to handle in his area but was not penalised and City subsequently launched the attack that created Semenyo’s second.

Régis Le Bris, Sunderland’s manager, said: “It was hard to see that as not a handball. It is what it is and we have to accept the decision. It’s hard to comment. It’s a defeat, but we are proud of the level of the squad. It is really tight at this level against one of the best teams in Europe. A half chance gets punished, and it’s probably the lesson of the day.”

Sports.title: Isak pounces to give Liverpool victory on Iraola’s return to Bournemouth
Sports.content:
At the final whistle, victory secured, Andoni Iraola embraced both his current players and those he guided to new heights at Bournemouth last season. Liverpool are not yet the overwhelming, suffocating force Iraola wants them to become but they did enough to claim three points here, Alexander Isak capping a peculiar performance with a simple finish.

Cody Gakpo was again the architect, the Dutchman the supplier for all four of Isak’s goals this season. Isak’s only other shot before scoring was to balloon a first-time effort high and wide but his second-half strike was sufficient to return Liverpool to winning ways in the Premier League.

Perhaps it was inevitable that these teams would neutralise each other. On Iraola’s final day at Bournemouth’s training base he spent an hour in the company of his successor, Marco Rose, who is yet to taste victory in the Premier League. The pair stopped talking only because Tiago Pinto, Bournemouth’s sporting director, interrupted to remind them there were other things on the agenda.

“We knew what we were going to get, they knew what they were going to get and maybe you could see it,” Rose said. “It is mostly the same after our games; I sit here after a good performance, but you don’t get points for good performances. You have to force wins.”

Amine Adli, sidelined because of a calf injury, scored a 95th-minute winner in a 3-2 victory for Bournemouth in this fixture last season but there was no such chaos to this game. The only clear sight of goal arrived approaching the hour when Gakpo bypassed Adrien Truffert down the right flank and squared, the ball trickling towards Isak on the edge of the six-yard box.

A few minutes earlier Isak had sent Iraola retreating to the away dugout. “Yes, yes,” Iraola said, encouraging Isak as the Sweden striker made tracks on the wing, white shirts attacking the box, only for his wayward cross to end up with the ball flying towards the scaffolding structure in a corner of this ground, part of Bournemouth’s ongoing stadium upgrade.

View image in fullscreen Andoni Iraola applauds the fans after victory at the Vitality Stadium. Photograph: Ian Walton/AP

In midweek, Iraola was rooting for his former club on their European bow but promised a businesslike return to Bournemouth and stepped off one of the two Liverpool team coaches with a game face. Tommy Elphick, who captained Bournemouth to the Premier League in 2015 and followed Iraola to Liverpool, embraced old colleagues pitchside before the warm-up.

“I love it because I love this club and it is growing,” Iraola said after Liverpool extended their unbeaten start to seven games in all competitions. “They will enjoy European nights here. This stadium will become a lot nicer. I was delighted to see a lot of the people I appreciate so much.”

All the niceties, Iraola said, could wait until afterwards. Pablo de la Torre, his fitness coach who was part of his Bournemouth staff, made that clear within the opening 30 seconds, wresting the ball away from Adam Smith to delay the hosts taking a quick throw‑in. Bournemouth were intent on building on their history‑making win on Thursday in the Basque Country and had the best chance of the first half, Alisson’s smart right-hand save preventing Evanilson’s front-post flick squeezing in at his near post.

Dominik Szoboszlai dropped a typically vicious free-kick wide of Djordje Petrovic’s post and Petrovic saved a deflected Bradley Barcola shot, but Liverpool spent much of the first half containing Bournemouth’s threats. Iraola conceded that his side were slow out of the blocks.

“We didn’t start with the intensity that is required to win here,” he said. “You never play comfortably here – Bournemouth put you under pressure and you have to adapt.”

Liverpool only teased glimpses of quality. Florian Wirtz saw a disguised pass for Isak cut out and Bournemouth flew forward, the alert and again impressive Jérémy Jacquet extinguishing the danger as Ryan Christie flung his body to connect with a low cross. Christie chopped inside Szoboszlai close to the touchline and Scott switched play with a pinged diagonal pass.

Bournemouth seemed to be growing in confidence but then Gakpo breezed past Truffert, usually such a dependable performer who last week was given a France recall. Gakpo crossed from the right and while James Hill dived in to stop the threat of Wirtz at the front post, the ball dropped to an unmarked Isak on the edge of the six‑yard box to stroke the ball in.

It was not a nerveless finale. Iraola hopped on the touchline as Scott, poised to make his England debut in this international window, lined up a 90th-minute free‑kick. After Liverpool won a free-kick deep into four minutes of stoppage time, Iraola crossed his hands and frantically pointed his players towards the scoreboard showing there were only a matter of seconds remaining. Moments later, it was a case of job done. “I think in life you always get what you deserve,” a phlegmatic Rose said. “One error is too much, that’s the point.”

Sports.title: Jonathan David earns Atlético precious win over 10-man Real Madrid in fractious derby
Sports.content:
On the eve of the derby, Diego Simeone described this as a special week in Madrid, a “tremendous energy about the city”, and it closed the way he wanted. He had enjoyed the Formula One, he said, and he had enjoyed seeing Shakira in concert, but he enjoyed this even more. At least he did by the time the last of many, many blows on the referee’s whistle brought it to an end, sprinting up the tunnel punching the air. Having been 2-0 up against 10 men through goals from Álex Grimaldo and Jonathan David, seemingly in control, a late header from Antonio Rüdiger awoke old ghosts and brought tension, but they did it.

José Mourinho’s first derby back at Real Madrid ended in defeat and recriminations: he turned up in the press conference with a picture of two moments in which he claimed that Lee Kang-in and Cristian Romero should have been sent off and insisted the story was there. And yet there are other questions: over the way Dean Huijsen gave away the penalty and got the red card that tilted the game against them, and how his team played, how little they did.

It is 13 years since these two managers met in this fixture, their last time the night Atlético won the Cup at the Santiago Bernabéu. Then, Mourinho was sent off and didn’t collect his medal from the king. His return has been driven by nostalgia and it was like old times in the press room. He and Simeone are “companions of war”, he had said, and so it was.

It was not until the 39th minute that there was a shot on target when Atlético’s Jan Oblak pushed Arda Guler’s long-range effort away. Otherwise, there was little football but it had been heating up from the beginning, Guler the first to confront the referee after a foul by Álex Baena. To which he responded by fouling Baena back. From the bench, something was said and Diego Simeone was booked; the scene had been set.

Atlético probed from wide, almost always the right wing. An advance on that side led to Ibrahima Konaté doubting and Giuliano Simeone flashing wide. At the other end Vinícius Júnior shot over twice before the half’s most significant moment. Which, appropriately, was not about the play.

Jude Bellingham slid in to tackle Romero and the referee showed him a yellow. Bellingham, his teammates and the bench were incensed and the video assistant referee was engaged. The referee Miguel Ángel Ortiz, struggling to control this, went to the screen where he saw Romero’s studs hit Bellingham’s knee. The decision was reversed, the Englishman’s yellow taken away and shown to the Argentinian instead. The hosts still felt it should have been red for Bellingham. When Lee’s studs went in on Federico Valverde’s ankle, Real did too. Confrontations continued, words exchanged, but chances didn’t come. At half-time Atlético’s goalkeeper coach and Real’s assistant were sent off.

The second half began with Koke introduced and Baena forcing a save. It was Atlético’s first shot on target and the start of a different game. Their second soon after gave them the lead and an advantage that was even bigger. A long ball from David Hancko dropped into the run of Simeone and as he dashed into the area Huijsen dragged him down. Ortiz pointed to the spot. He was also called to the screen again – not to overturn the penalty but to change the colour of the card. Huijsen walked, Grimaldo scored and the Metropolitano exploded.

View image in fullscreen Real Madrid’s Dean Huijsen fouls Giuliano Simeone leading to a penalty and a red card for the defender. Photograph: Juan Carlos Lucas/Zuma Press Wire/Shutterstock

You suspected Mourinho would too. First, he removed Guler and Vinícius to introduce Yan Diomandé and Rüdiger. Vinícius had done little and a readjustment was required but there have been times when decisions like this – the Brazilian’s removal in last year’s clásico was the beginning of the end for Xabi Alonso – have caused splits. It did not improve things either. Instead, Real were oddly passive and Atlético doubled the lead. It came from the right where Lee, outstanding, worked the ball to Simeone. His low cross, bent behind Madrid’s back four, was perfect. Six yards out, David turned it in.

Still Atlético came. Courtois made an extraordinary save from Romero and Konaté cleared off the line from Julián Alvarez. Real could do nothing, seemingly concerned only with limiting the damage. Oblak barely saw them. Real did not touch the ball in his area until they scored. Kylian Mbappé barely touched the ball anywhere. Inside Atlético’s half, a pigeon pecked the grass, uninterrupted.

When Diomandé did at last dash into that space with 15 minutes to go, Oblak saved, the opportunity to make a match of this wasted. Or so it seemed until, from a dead ball that was too late even for them, Rüdiger headed in to spark a rebellion that would prove brief and incomplete, unlike Simeone’s week.

Sports.title: ‘Mixed emotions’ for Farke as Leeds stay unbeaten with Crystal Palace stalemate
Sports.content:
Perhaps it is testament to the progress Leeds have made since returning to the Premier League just over a year ago that there was frustration at failing to move up to third after drawing with Crystal Palace. Instead, Daniel Farke’s team enter the prolonged international break in fifth and unbeaten, which is a fine achievement in itself.

Apart from Tyrick Mitchell’s disallowed goal, neither side gave much impression they would secure the points. For Palace, it was a first clean sheet of the season, having conceded at least twice in their opening four games, relieving pressure on Pierre Sage, while the hosts endured their first blank.

A victory by two clear goals would have meant a best-ever start to a Premier League campaign for Leeds but they were blunt in the final third. There was even a level of discontent amid a ponderous performance with fans chanting “forward” as they failed to replicate the thrashing of Newcastle on Monday.

“Mixed emotions,” Farke said. “We would have preferred to win, but the reality is it is 38 game days. It is not always magic nights under the floodlights, champagne football, you overrun the opponent and score goals for fun. Sometimes it is a scruffy Sunday afternoon when you have to dig in. This was one of these games.”

Farke is into the final year of his contract and signing a new deal is a priority for him and the club. His stature has grown over the past 10 months, with Leeds the fifth-best performing team in the division since December 2025 and the German will likely be rewarded in the coming weeks for bringing stability to the club as Leeds aim to build on strong foundations.

The most notable moment of the opening quarter here came when Walter Benítez took too long to distribute the ball. The referee, Adam Herczeg – making his Premier League debut and fully aware of the rules – awarded Leeds a corner as punishment. It was a tentative game in the autumn sunshine, lacking intensity and quality, with Ao Tanaka snatching at a shot the closest anyone got to threatening a goal.

Around the half-hour something akin to a football match broke out as nervousness was replaced by urgency. Jørgen Strand Larsen and Quinten Timber engineered a chance for Palace which was blocked and allowed Leeds to break through Noah Okafor down the left, although his cross was turned behind.

Palace had the greater quality, with Adam Wharton and Timber comfortable in possession in the middle of the park, while Yéremy Pino whizzed around in the hope of finding an opener. It was controlled play, as the visitors took their time in the buildup, although there was often very little at the end of it as James Trafford was left unthreatened.

View image in fullscreen James Justin stretches to block an effort from Eddie Nketiah. Photograph: Greig Cowie/Shutterstock

Leeds on the other hand would burst into life for brief moments as the full-backs flew forward, changing the dynamic in an instant but Palace’s centre-backs and wing-backs were built to deal with these rapid transitions, leaving Dominic Calvert-Lewin starved of service. Benítez could relax and re-read the laws of the game, having failed to face a single shot on target in the opening 40 minutes.

Palace pushed the fast-forward button at the break and Mitchell put the ball in the back of the net from a fine move down the right. The glory turned to anguish when the video assistant referee intervened to show Anan Khalaili was offside in the buildup, causing an eruption inside Elland Road.

Leeds were sluggish but the warning from Mitchell caused a reaction and they were almost ahead when Calvert-Lewin’s only real chance was saved by Benítez. The England striker was given too much space to get on the end of a cross but his sidefooted volley was weak.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

There was a touch of menace in the game as Tanaka and Wharton were booked in quick succession, the first for a cynical foul and the latter after lunging in late without a hope of winning the ball, ensuring Herczeg was far busier than the two goalkeepers.

Leeds were completely ineffective in open play, Ethan Ampadu engaged in a long-throwathon. Every few minutes he would trot to a sidelineto pick up the ball and hurl it into the box but Palace were alive to the danger. “We had many set pieces today, but also today we didn’t have the best quality of the delivery,” Farke said.

Palace edged the match and Daichi Kamada could have won it late on but his header drifted inches wide. Sage will be relieved to see his defence so well organised and untroubled after conceding 11 in the first four games, leading to plenty of early scrutiny on his appointment. “Especially when I read the social media, there’s a big pressure.” Sage said.

“But you know, I don’t care about that. I do my job with honesty, I give my best with my skills and my limits. And in the end, I have no regrets with what I do.”

Sports.title: Rangers and Ryan Naderi finish off Celtic’s horror week with Old Firm victory
Sports.content:
If ever a stadium can be rocked by silence, this was the moment. With no visiting fans allowed at any of this season’s Glasgow derbies, Ryan Naderi’s winning goal was met with nothing but the banging of fists of the clear plastic of the Rangers bench, and the shouting of the broadcast commentators. A screaming void of apathy and atrophy, the sound of a beckoning abyss, of a title race blowing open and a team slowly breaking apart.

That Rangers were unable to celebrate this triumph with their fans in the stadium was, of course, a source of lament, as well as a measure of just how ugly this fixture has become over the years.

It has become a day that is no longer relished but dreaded, a failure not just of the two fanbases themselves but the authorities who have allowed the ugliness to fester, who have talked a tough game on sectarianism but done little in practice to combat it at source.

But nothing could spoil the mood of Derek McInnes’s team, humming after a tough start to the season and now able to toast a second victory over their rivals in the space of a week. For Celtic, sitting on three straight defeats, the silence will be filled with plenty of noises and voices over the coming international break: awkward questions and painful decisions that last season’s dramatic double may have forestalled but which can no longer be avoided.

The drop in standards over the opening weeks of this season has been alarming, and at 74 years of age Martin O’Neill is wise enough and self-aware enough to know that he may be as much part of the problem as part of the solution. For him, the next few weeks will be a time of “self-reflection” on his role and his future, on whether he truly has the energy in him for one last fight.

“It’s a matter of whether I can help the team, and I’ll have a look at that this week,” he said. “Every time things don’t go so well, age plays a part, and you know what, they may be right. I’m 110 in two years’ time. That may be time to wrap it up. But I’ll see how it goes.

View image in fullscreen Tempers flare between Rangers manager Derek McInnes (right) and his opposite number, Martin O’Neill, at Celtic Park. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

“Let me generalise a little bit. I got an opportunity to come back last October which I never thought would happen in my life. Winning the league, the game against Hearts, was one of the great moments of my managerial time. But even then, I was still thinking about whether you can still have the energy, the desire. There’s nothing great about getting old, I’ll tell you that.”

What is true of O’Neill may also be true of a few of his players. Is Callum McGregor, club legend but now 33 years of age and increasingly off the pace, still fit for purpose? Does Liam Scales need replacing? Does Kieran Tierney still have the legs? What exactly is James Forrest still doing about the place? And in the meantime, would you remotely trust the Celtic board – still essentially hollow of footballing expertise – to oversee the required transition?

Not on this evidence. The summer signings – Kasper Høgh, Mika Baur, Camilo Durán – largely disappeared from view.
