Quick Guide Roundup: Vrancken bewildered by VAR as Hearts frustrated at Kilmarnock Show Wouter Vrancken was left bewildered by the “strange” video assistant referee decision to rule out an early Hearts goal in their 1-1 draw at bottom-placed Kilmarnock. The Jambos thought they had gone ahead in the 11th minute when Laurent Mendy’s effort – which appeared to be going wide – was diverted into the net by the Killie defender Cathal McCarthy. But the VAR, Matthew MacDermid, advised Duncan Nicolson to rule it out as the ball had accidentally struck Mendy’s hand. Killie went ahead a few minutes later through a Jamie McCart own goal before Stephen Kingsley equalised in the 86th minute (pictured). But Vrancken cited similarities with the recent incident involving Manchester United’s Harry Maguire against Ipswich and felt Mendy’s inadvertent handball should have been rendered irrelevant by McCarthy heading the ball into the net. “For me, when it’s such a clear situation, it’s strange that the VAR comes in between and rules wrong,” said the Belgian. “We had a meeting last week about the laws of the game and the refs did their explanation but when you don’t see them applied in the game, then I’m thinking this is strange." Martin Boyle ended Hibernian’s losing streak at home after they fought back to claim a point in a 1-1 draw against Aberdeen. The Dons went ahead in the 17th minute with a composed finish from former Hibs striker Kevin Nisbet. Managerless Hibs – with John Potter in interim charge after David Gray’s midweek sacking – looked bereft of confidence for long spells. However, the Leith side – who had lost six successive games at Easter Road – earned a share of the spoils when Boyle levelled from the penalty spot in the 62nd minute after Jack Milne dragged Jason Kerr to the ground. Steven Pressley praised Joe Westley for the bravery he showed by playing in Dundee's 2-1 home win over Motherwell. The former Burnley striker fractured his cheekbone against Hearts a fortnight ago but declared himself available after deciding against having surgery. Instead, he played wearing a protective mask and nett Dundee’s opening goal from the penalty spot before Bradley Fink doubled their advantage. Alex Lowry pulled one back for the visitors just before the break but the home side held on. Pressley said: “Joe showed great courage. But he gave a wonderful performance, without any trepidation. Joe was fearless in everything he did and to score a goal is really important for him because he lives off them." Jim Goodwin hailed his side’s performance as the perfect tonic as Dundee United defeated St Mirren 3-0 in a one-sided contest in Paisley, with first-half goals from Jesse Randall, Lyall Cameron and Kevin Ciubotaru. It was Goodwin’s first appearance in the dugout since a recent health scare and the United manager said: “On a personal note, it was great to be back. Certainly the best medicine that I could have hoped for was that type of result and performance." A stunning set-piece strike from Enes Alic in the sixth minute of stoppage time secured a dramatic 1-1 draw for 10-man St Johnstone against Falkirk. Falkirk took advantage of Cheick Diabaté’s 54th-minute red card to seize the lead through Ethan Ross on the hour. But Alic found the top corner from 25 yards to move Simo Valakari’s side up to sixth place. Press Association Photograph: Mark Runnacles/Shutterstock Editorial Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

There was fury here but precious little focus, plenty of passion but no real patterns of play, no order to the chaos, no real idea of how to keep the ball or fashion a chance. Rangers dominated the central areas, where Dan Neil and Nicolas Raskin are already forging a formidable partnership and James Penrice merrily stomped all over the place.

O’Neill gambled on a back five, on Luke McCowan in a sort of withdrawn winger role, discarded both at half-time, rolled through his substitutions, but the plan never really emerged from the fog. Celtic are basically like the tangled ball of printer cables and headphone wires in the bottom drawer, where you’re never quite sure whether you’re unpicking the knots or making them tighter.

Naderi’s goal, bundled in from close range after Kim Min-su’s long-range effort was parried helpfully into his path by Viljami Sinisalo, was simply the most consequential emblem of Rangers’ superiority here. Emmanuel Fernandez got a rough ride early on, Tierney clipped the bar from distance and Ivor Pandur made a fine save from Colby Donovan early in the second half. That was basically it, as far as explicit threat went. Donovan’s header was the only Celtic shot on target.

“For a young team, it’s brilliant that they can take the good from this,” said McInnes. “Coming to places like this, it won’t get much more difficult. It’s only three points, but in the context of the season it was important for lots of reasons.” He knows, of course, that Rangers are not the finished article. But right now there is a power vacuum at the top of Scottish football and his improving side may as well be the one to fill it.

Sports.title: ‘We miss her the same every day’: Olivia Cusack on her late footballer sister Maddy
Sports.content:
Olivia Cusack says her sister, the late Maddy Cusack, is on her mind every single day and she is determined to ensure her “legacy lives on” three years after the former England youth international midfielder’s death.

Olivia, together with family and friends of Maddy, walked 29 miles from Bramall Lane, Sheffield United’s home, to their family’s home in Horsley, near Derby, on Saturday to raise funds and awareness. Maddy’s loved ones are still enduring a “frustrating and confusing” wait for answers about the circumstances surrounding her death on 20 September 2023.

An inquest into the death of the 27-year-old Sheffield United player was adjourned again in July and has been scheduled to resume on 7 December after fresh evidence came to light. Cusack, a former England under-19 international, was the first player to appear in 100 matches for the Sheffield United women’s team.

Olivia says the walk on Saturday, “Bringing Maddy Home”, was motivated by some of the evidence during the inquest. “After the inquest we wanted to bring her home from Bramall Lane, back to our family home,” she says. “Many people know Maddy as the professional football player and the name on the back of her shirt, the number, the colours she wore, the club she was associated with.

“But I felt in the inquest it was lost that she was a person, she wasn’t an object that we were discussing. She’s a person, she’s a family member of ours [and] a person that’s sometimes been lost within the chaos surrounding her death really, so that’s the notion behind the walk. To claim her back, bring her home and protect her.”

A minute’s applause will be held before kick-off on Sunday at the Women’s Super League 2 fixture between Newcastle and Sheffield United. Discussing that anniversary, Olivia says: “We miss her the same every day, as I will on Sunday. The anniversary is always something that creeps up on us. It’s very emotional and it’s a time where we just reflect, but we do so much throughout the year so she really is at the heart of pretty much every single day. Not a day goes by where we don’t think about her.

View image in fullscreen Sheffield United and Maddy Cusack’s family paid tribute at Bramall Lane shortly after her death. Photograph: Richard Callis/MB Media/Getty Images

“There can be days when you just feel absolutely drained and you know you don’t quite know what the right thing to do is, but I think the way that we just get through it is that we remember who she was as a person. She loved her life, she loved trying new things and just enjoying life’s simple pleasures, we try and embody that on every day, not just the anniversary.

“I really do encourage people to, as difficult as it can be sometimes, share the photos, share the memories, bring her up in conversation wherever you can, talk about her, and between all of us, you know her legacy will live on.”

The family have already endured eight full days of evidence, after the hearing began belatedly on 29 June, but the discovery of additional documents led the proceedings to be paused until December. The coroner apologised to the family for yet another delay. The case had been set previously to start being heard on 5 January 2026 after additional postponements in 2025.

“It’s been really difficult,” Olivia said of the delays. “It’s not something that any of us anticipated to happen. It’s very confusing and it can be very frustrating, the length of time it’s taken, it can be difficult to work that out and to know how you should be feeling and the process of it. However, we know that for the right outcome it has to be taken seriously. They need the time to come together and really get an outcome.

View image in fullscreen Maddy Cusack was also remembered during the Premier League match between Sheffield United and Newcastle. Photograph: George Wood/Getty Images

“It feels as though she can’t be at peace until it’s finished. And I do feel that’s quite upsetting to think about and to work through. It needs to come to a conclusion.”

Olivia said she would “channel Maddy’s energy” during the 29-mile walk on Saturday, when a group of about 15 family and friends travelled in the reverse direction to another fundraising walk in February 2024 from Pride Park to Bramall Lane.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

This time they set off from Sheffield at 5.30am. A fundraising page for the walk had surpassed £1,100 as of Saturday afternoon. Olivia described that tally as “incredible – £1,000 is just amazing, it’s more than I ever expected” and said: “Particularly with it being Maddy’s anniversary, it’s going to be very much a mental challenge as well as a physical one, so it gives you that extra motivation to make the people who’ve donated proud.”

The money is being raised for the Maddy Cusack Foundation, which is helping a range of causes targeting women’s and girls’ football and “letting girls be seen within sport”.

“We provided Derby County Community Trust with a series of bursaries for girls and families who struggle with the financial prospects of becoming dedicated to their football. It’s a helping hand for any child that needs that extra sort of funding, taking away the barriers that they might face.”

The foundation has also partnered with the Stockport County left wing-back and former Derby, Sheffield United and Nottingham Forest player defender Ben Osborn’s organisation Elite Football Development, which aims to inspire young people through sport and education.

“They work with girls and boys but we sponsor the girls’ side of things, which is focused around post-16 study, and allows girls to gain qualifications alongside being able to train and live the life of a professional footballer. We were really keen to get involved in this as Maddy was really passionate about education.”

In the UK and Ireland, Samaritans can be contacted on freephone 116 123. In the US, you can call or text the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline on 988, chat on 988lifeline.org, or text HOME to 741741 to connect with a crisis counsellor. In Australia, the crisis support service Lifeline is 13 11 14. Other international helplines can be found at befrienders.org

Sports.title: Hayen must worry about his Burnley future but fans’ fears are existential
Sports.content:
The greatest moments of Burnley’s history were beamed on to a big screen before kick-off at Turf Moor, accompanied by famous lines of commentary. The final one, the moment promotion was sealed under Scott Parker in April 2025, was soundtracked by: “Burnley are back in the big time.” That feels a long time ago now, with a return to the Premier League a remote prospect.

Burnley appeared to have this game against Derby sewn up, leading through Zeki Amdouni’s first-half header, but a stunning stoppage-time strike from the Rams’ substitute Mo Fuseini soured the Turf Moor mood. It means Burnley’s winless home league run could now reach a year, the Clarets last tasting victory at Turf Moor on 18 October 2025. Their last win in any competition in 90 minutes was on 11 February.

The draw left Nicky Hayen, the under-fire head coach, under scrutiny, though the majority of fans will direct their anger towards Alan Pace, the chair, given the financial problems and off-field turmoil that plagued the club during a disruptive summer.

Hayen vowed to fight for his future and revealed he would talk with Pace, though could give no assurances he will remain in charge for the next game at Watford on 10 October after the extra-long international break. “I can understand the fans are angry after a start like this, it’s not what they want to see from their team or from myself,” he said. “It’s my responsibility. But I’ve always shown resilience and I’m always going to fight. We need this [international] window to change a lot of things.”

View image in fullscreen Mohammed Fuseini celebrates scoring a late equaliser for Derby. Photograph: Alfie Carling/PPAUK/Shutterstock

In his programme notes before the game, Pace called for fans to “unite and show togetherness”, after they had chanted for his removal during the home defeat by Bristol City a fortnight ago. There was some early encouragement for Hayen’s team as they sought to make inroads against Derby. Although a lack of thrust in the final third was evident at times, Burnley made the breakthrough via Amdouni’s forehead, the forward peeling around the back post to nod home Lucas Pires’s corner.

Hayen, who was managing Haverfordwest County in the Welsh Premier four years ago and was not Burnley’s first choice to replace Parker, celebrated. Having been accused of muddled selections in his tenure so far, he had made some brave calls, dropping the club captain, Kyle Walker, and struggling goalkeeper Max Weiss, and recalling Marcus Edwards, who had been jettisoned after featuring in the campaign’s opening two games.

Those decisions were nearly vindicated, right up to the moment Fuseini pounced, leaving Hayen to bear the brunt of more fan criticism. “It is really difficult [to take],” he said. “You saw the reaction of the players after the game, sitting on the ground, disappointed. We wanted to give the fans the win, I wanted this for them, I can accept their frustration. I want to give back to the fans, I feel we can give back a lot. You saw we were close, we wanted to do it just before the international break.”

Quick Guide López fires Wolves to derby win over West Brom Show Fer López fired Wolves to a 1-0 win against arch rivals West Brom in a bruising Black Country derby on Sunday. Lopez punished a blunder by Albion defender Nat Phillips to score his fifth goal of the season in the second half of the Championship clash at Molineux. It was no more than Wolves deserved after Albion keeper Max O’Leary had kept West Brom in the game during the first half with three outstanding saves. Albion rarely threatened to snatch an equaliser in the first Molineux meeting between the west midlands rivals in five years. After fears of a repeat of the serious crowd trouble that marred their previous showdown at West Brom two years ago, the derby passed off peacefully inside the stadium. Elsewhere in the Championship, Bolton twice came from behind to win 4-3 in a thriller at Norwich. Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

The break may represent a chance for Hayen, if he remains, to regroup, though for Pace and the board there remain unanswered questions about the £142m of external debt the club owes, as well as the £81m owed by his firm ALK Capital to the club itself after a leveraged buyout in December 2020. Comparisons with the Glazers’ takeover and ownership of Manchester United have been made. James Holroyd’s recent departure, after 15 months as chief executive, feels reflective of the worsening malaise in the boardroom. Holroyd previously worked under the Glazers at United.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Despite two promotions under the current regime (and three relegations) the Clarets’ financial situation has deteriorated, with some fans now harbouring genuine fears of total extinction if debts are not repaid. Parachute payments may help for a time, but Burnley no longer have the cash reserves they boasted in their debt-free era before Pace and ALK when they enjoyed five successive seasons in the Premier League under Sean Dyche. Such stability now feels a world away and problems are spilling on to the pitch. Money has been spent on transfers, with squad turnover high in recent seasons, but there was particular concern when the £20m made from the sale of Zian Flemming was not reinvested in a new striker, with 39-year-old Jamie Vardy hastily arriving on a free transfer after the transfer window had closed.

View image in fullscreen Zeki Amdouni sprints off to celebrate his goal for Burnley. Photograph: Alfie Carling/PPAUK/Shutterstock

Hayen sent on Vardy and loan signing Largie Ramazani to retain a counterattacking threat against Derby late on, as Burnley hung on. But with a slender lead going into stoppage time, their confidence appeared brittle. Goalkeeper Grégoire Coudert had been forced into a couple of late interventions after Ryan Hedges should have equalised for Derby on the hour mark.

Then, just when it seemed Burnley’s winless streak would be broken, the rocket from Fuseini snatched two points away, leaving them bottom of the Championship. “It’s hard to take,” said Hayen. “It’s frustrating.”

Sports.title: Fuming Alvaro Arbeloa accuses Premier League referees of 'not wanting Man United to lose' - claiming 'EVERY decision' went their way in last-gasp draw against Fulham
Sports.content:
Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa's furious rant is set to land him an FA sanction after he claimed officials 'would not let Man United lose' during Sunday's 1-1 draw.

The Cottagers looked set to see out a famous win over United until Matheus Cunha's late deflected strike salvaged a barely-deserved point for Michael Carrick's side.

At the heart of Arbeloa's annoyance was the fact that he felt the foul awarded to United, adjudged on Harry Maguire, 35 seconds before Cunha scored was unjust and ultimately cost Fulham three points.

In his immediate post-match comments, Arbeloa could barely contain his anger.

'Every decision was for them and I knew after the game against Man City that they would not let Man Utd lose. We deserved a little bit more,' Arbeloa said.

'We were so, so close. We were a little bit unlucky again. We knew it would be difficult against this big team.

'We knew what happened last week. We have seen what the referee has been doing in all the matches, so it was a difficult game. And we were unlucky.'

Alvaro Arbeloa claimed that match officials 'did not want Man United to lose' on Sunday

Matheus Cunha's late deflected strike cost Fulham three points, leaving Arbeloa fuming

Perhaps there had been a word in Arbeloa's ear before his post-match press conference with journalists as he looked to tone down his criticism.

'My English is not so good,' Arbeloa said.

'Maybe I explain myself so bad and I prefer not to say anything about the referees because you never know.'

Arbeloa's initial rant will almost certainly land him in hot water with the FA as questioning the integrity of match officials or alleging bias is a surefire way to land a hefty fine, or even touchline ban.

Former Fulham boss Marco Silva fell foul of this rule previously, as have many of Arbeloa's peers.

The result, while not a precious win, is still a step in the right direction for Fulham, who lifted themselves off the foot of the table, condemning Tottenham Hotspur to last place for the first time since 2009.

Sports.title: Raheem Sterling vows to be 'better than yesterday' as former England footballer, 31, breaks his silence after pleading guilty to dangerous driving and drug possession following £270,000 Lamborghini car crash
Sports.content:
Raheem Sterling says he is seeking 'progress over perfection' after pleading guilty to dangerous driving and drug possession.

In his first Instagram post since bodycam footage of his May arrest was released, Sterling says his goal is to 'be better than yesterday'.

On Tuesday, Sterling pleaded guilty at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court after crashing his £270,000 Lamborghini while driving under the influence of laughing gas.

Sterling told police he had 'a problem' with the drug after submitting rush hour motorists to a terrifying 90 minutes of dangerous driving, in which he zig-zagged on the M25 and M3 motorways before swerving onto a slip road and crashing into a metal gate.

The 31-year-old former England international was arrested by police who claim he tried to hide nitrous oxide, or laughing gas, from them by moving it to the back seat of his black Lamborghini Urus SUV.

Police bodycam footage shows the moment that Sterling was arrested with canisters and a deflated balloon on his lap. An officer can be heard saying 'you can put that down' to the footballer after opening his car door.

He can then be seen taking the items from his lap and putting them behind his seat.

Raheem Sterling says he is seeking 'progress over perfection' following his court case

Sterling pleaded guilty to dangerous driving and drug possession after crashing his £270,000 Lamborghini in May

The 31-year-old was charged with dangerous driving and possession of laughing gas after swerving his car on the M25 and M3

Sterling is asked 'can you jump out for me' and who was at the wheel at the time of the crash, but does not reply.

The officer adds: 'So you refuse to answer, okay.'

Sterling is told to get out of the car, asked his name and age at the roadside and to 'put the phone down, stop playing games. Stop tensing up.'

The former Manchester City and Chelsea star, who won the PFA Young Player of the Year award in 2018-19, is then read his rights as he is arrested after being asked to put his arms behind his back.

His arrest, near the Minley interchange on the M3 in Hampshire, happened four weeks after he had returned to the UK following the end of an abortive attempt to revive his football career at Dutch club Feyenoord. He remains without a club.

Sterling, from Berkshire, pleaded guilty on Tuesday to dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen after a single vehicle collision at 8.45am on May 28. Police found six cannisters of nitrous oxide in his car.

Basingstoke Magistrates' Court heard that Sterling was so impaired by the laughing gas that he was unable to perform basic police station tests like placing his finger on his nose or placing one foot in front of another.

Barrister Simon Jones, prosecuting, said of Sterling: 'He appeared to be quiet, withdrawn and lethargic and actively fidgeting. Eye lids drooping consistent with fatigue or drug impairment. He said he was feeling very cold, despite this being in the middle of a heatwave with 33-degree temperatures.'

Motorist Fiona Jennings told police she had looked across to witness the driver of the Lamborghini with a balloon in front of his face which was so big she thought it was an air bag.

Image issued by the Crown Prosecution Service shows the damage to the Lamborghini Urus being driven by Sterling

The former England international was pictured arriving in court today to face charges following a car crash in May

Sterling, from Berkshire, pleaded guilty on Tuesday to dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen

It was so big that 'she had no idea how the driver would have been able to see the road ahead,' Mr Jones said. Ms Jennings described Sterling's driving as 'absolutely horrendous' and expressed 'genuine concern that the driver may kill someone.'

Evidence presented to court suggested Sterling was also inhaling laughing gas while at the wheel of the Lamborghini a full seven hours before his arrest.

A concerned witness called police after seeing the driver of the same car entering a McDonalds car park alarmingly fast at 1.10am the same morning and seeing the driver holding up 'a pink, inflated balloon.'

By 7.45am that morning, another motorist concerned by the Lamborghini erratically changing lanes, saw the driver placing a white balloon to his mouth and inhaling its contents. For 30 minutes, that motorist watched the vehicle weave from inside to outside lane and back and come close to smashing into the central reservation.

It was after Sterling had left the M3 near Farnborough, Hampshire, hit the gate and come to halt with the tyres of his wheels ripped up, that police found him sitting in T-shirt and shorts in the passenger seat of the car.

One officer told him to 'stop tensing up' after he had stepped out of the car. Sterling replied: 'I'm not tensing up.' Sterling provided breath tests, which established he was not under the influence of cannabis, cocaine or alcohol. But he later refused requests for a blood test, insisting that a lawyer of his choosing must be present, having rejected the offer of a duty solicitor. He also refused to answer any police questions.

Mr Jones said of Sterling's conduct: 'He was attempting to impose a condition on provision of a specimen. He was told the investigation could not be delayed for that reason. At the roadside, there was cooperation without the need for legal advice. When the search for the presence of drugs started, the cooperation ended.'

Sterling's barrister, Jason Bartfeld QC, told the court that there was 'extensive personal mitigation' in his case and that the footballer had taken 'voluntary steps to mitigate his difficulties.'

Mr Bartfeld agreed that this was a 'top category case' because it was a prolonged period of dangerous driving and Sterling was suffering 'serious impairment'. But he said the nitrous oxide would only have caused impairment in 'short periods' and that the chemical did not pose the same risks as cannabis or alcohol.

He claimed police had left Sterling confused about the blood sample. Sterling later told police in a statement: 'I asked for a solicitor. I did not fully understand I had not slept all night and was tired and confused.'

Sterling could face a maximum two years' imprisonment. The case was adjourned until November for pre-sentencing reports.

Sports.title: Furious Gary Neville rips into Man United's 'walking' stars and tells Michael Carrick to STOP defending them after 'absolutely pathetic' draw with Fulham: 'Worst 15 minutes I've EVER seen'
Sports.content:
Furious Gary Neville rips into Man United's 'walking' stars and tells Michael Carrick to STOP defending them after 'absolutely pathetic' draw with Fulham: 'Worst 15 minutes I've EVER seen'

Gary Neville branded Manchester United’s lack of effort ‘an absolute disgrace’ after their insipid 1-1 draw against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

Matheus Cunha’s deflected effort in the 89th minute rescued United from a third defeat in a week, but even the Brazilian admitted that his team didn’t try hard enough.

United go into the international break in 12th place with five points – their joint-lowest total after five games of the season in the Premier League era.

Former United defender Neville fumed on Sky Sports: ‘I rarely say teams don't make an effort because that's the ultimate criticism. That first 15 minutes of the second half, and generally the first 60 minutes, United were an absolute disgrace.

‘I’ve watched Man United since the age of five and that's the worst 15 minutes I've ever seen. Absolutely pathetic. I've never seen such a lack of effort.

‘There needs to be a reset in terms of structure. They don't want to do the ugly part of the game.

Gary Neville branded Manchester United an 'absolute disgrace' for their perceived lack of effort during their 1-1 draw with Fulham

Michael Carrick defended his men, who have made the joint-worst start to a season in the club's Premier League history

‘I've never seen a Manchester United team walk as much as that. Michael (Carrick) needs to stop defending them.

'If they carry on like that, they will concede so many goals week after week. They were lucky to concede one.

'I just see apathy and ambling around the pitch. They can all work harder than that- they're getting outrun in every match.'

After Cunha scored a late equaliser – heavily deflected off David Affengruber – to cancel out a disastrous own-goal by team-mate Lisandro Martinez, the forward admitted that United only woke up once Fulham went ahead.

‘In the second half it was like they put in more energy than us,’ he said. ‘We cannot accept this. We always play better after conceding a goal, and it cannot be like this.’

In United's defence, they came up against an inspired goalkeeper in Bernd Leno, who made five saves and won man of the match.

Lisandro Martinez, Bryan Mbeumo, and Marcus Rashford were all denied by the German, while Bruno Fernandes and Cunha hit the post.

Fulham's opener was unfortunate but not undeserved, as Calvin Bassey's shot comically deflected in off Lisandro Martinez and Senne Lammens.

Manchester United had 25 shots but were accused of lacking defensive effort by Neville

Goalscorer Matheus Cunha admitted that Fulham had 'more energy' than the Red Devils

Carrick attempted to defend his men at full time, telling Sky Sports: 'We should have won the game, we created enough. We had a lot of good play. The goal that we did concede is one of them goals.

'The boys could've thought it was one of those days and that it went against us, but I really liked the reaction. We nearly won it at the end.

'We came to get the win, the way the game has panned out and the reaction is the positive we take from it.

'Their goalkeeper, the saves that he's made, he's made three top saves, arguably man of the match. That tells you how much we worked him. We hit the post twice and had a lot of opportunities. There's things to take from it.

'I don't think we were (passive). Do you think we were passive?'

Told that his team didn't have any shots in the first 15 minutes of the second half, he hit back: 'That doesn't mean we were passive. It's the Premier League, you're going to have spells where you don't have it all your own way.'

Asked if he was satisfied with his team's energy levels, Carrick said: 'Yeah.'

He added: 'We can take a lot and learn a lot from today. We need to be better and we will be.'

Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa was denied his first Premier League win, and accused referee Peter Bankes of favouring United.

‘There were so many things for them,’ said Arbeloa. ‘Every decision was for them. I knew after the game against Manchester City that they (referees) don't like Manchester United to lose.

‘We were so, so close to our first victory that we are a little bit upset now.’

Sports.title: Celtic supporters' bus bursts into FLAMES: Emergency services rush to scene in Glasgow to evacuate fans after Old Firm derby
Sports.content:
Celtic supporters' bus bursts into FLAMES: Emergency services rush to scene in Glasgow to evacuate fans after Old Firm derby

A group of football fans suffered a major scare as their coach went up in flames following Sunday's Old Firm derby.

As frustrated Celtic fans headed for home having seen their side lose 1-0 at Parkhead to their bitterest rivals Rangers, the biggest concern of the day was still to come.

As a group of Celtic fans travelled home the rear of their coach caught fire on the A728 near to the Emirates Arena.

Thick black smoke soon dominated the Glasgow sky as fans were quickly evacuated and moved to safety as emergency services rushed to the scene in the east end of the city.

Police Scotland have confirmed nobody was injured.

But in a latest twist, McLean's Coaches, who own, the coach, believe 'vandalism' caused the fire.

A group of Celtic fans were evacuated as their coach home burst into flames after the match

A statement from McLean's Coaches, shared by the Daily Record, after the fire claimed: 'We are aware of an incident involving one of our coaches on the Clyde Gateway earlier today. Based on the initial information and images we have received, we have reason to believe the incident may have been caused by vandalism.

'The matter has been reported to the relevant authorities, who are investigating the circumstances. The vehicle has been recovered and will undergo a full inspection.'

Two fire engines were seen on site with the Clyde Gateway brought to a standstill as the blaze was tackled and eventually halted with stunned fans watching on from the side of the road.

It marked the end to a disappointing day for those rooting for Celtic after they were narrowly beaten.

Ryan Naderi's first half strike was enough by the time the final whistle sounded as Celtic's misery was compounded by the fact that they have now lost to Rangers twice in the space of eight days.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher insists £116m Liverpool star Florian Wirtz must be DROPPED by Andoni Iraola after his 'poorest performance' in a Reds shirt against Bournemouth
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher believes Florian Wirtz must be dropped by Liverpool after 'one of his poorest' performances in a red shirt at Bournemouth.

The £116million attacker has flattered to deceive since pitching up from Bayer Leverkusen and Liverpool legend Carragher was left totally unimpressed with his showing on the south coast.

'That was one of the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt,' Carragher, said, speaking on the new Jamie Carragher Podcast.

'I've been critical of the fact that he hasn't got the numbers. But normally when you watch Wirtz, he's neat and tidy, he keeps possession, there's things that you like. He gets out of a tight situation where you're normally expecting your player to lose the ball.

'But the reason I worry is, I don't think Wirtz is in poor form since he came to Liverpool. I actually think what we're seeing is what he is.'

Carragher's comments laid bare just how little Wirtz has done to convince of his talents in England, with the Sky pundit adding that he simply doesn't see 'how he's going to hurt' teams.

Florian Wirtz (left) needs to be dropped when Liverpool face Man City, says Jamie Carragher

Wirtz (right) once again struggled to exert any influence when Liverpool faced Bournemouth

'The gap he's got to get to almost justify what people were expecting, I almost think is too big. You can't get there,' Carragher added as part of his damning assessment.

'Even if he improves a bit and gets there, it's still not what Liverpool thought they were getting.

'And it's not just Wirtz, it's the knock-on effect. So when he plays at No 10, it means Dominik Szoboszlai has to play central midfield. I don't think Szoboszlai is a central-midfield player, I don't.'

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola now goes into a three-week international break with plenty ponder ahead of a return to action against league leaders Manchester City on October 11.

'I think going forward Iraola's got a decision to make here. Wirtz would not be in my Liverpool team,' Carragher added.

'I thought this Bournemouth game was a big game for Wirtz. Because if he doesn't produce [against Bournemouth], he's then going to have a three-week break.

'By the time we come back, we're into October. Before you know it, it'll be Christmas in six to eight weeks, or it'll feel like we're getting to Christmas. He has to do something!

'Wirtz wouldn't be in my Liverpool team. Manchester City at home, for me, he can't be in the team.'

Sports.title: How Led Zeppelin-loving anglophile from Los Angeles, who worships Jeremy Clarkson, beat Rory McIlroy to land PGA title, as Spanish outsider chokes to miss out on £1.3m prize
Sports.content:
For JJ Spaun, the Led Zeppelin-loving anglophile from Los Angeles, there was a fairway to heaven at the BMW Championship. For Rory McIlroy, a resident on the Wentworth estate, there was a near miss and a short journey home to process it.

Whatever difficulties McIlroy is experiencing with his swing, he was sufficiently grooved to card a 68 and a 15-under-par finish that left the world No2 two strokes behind Spaun.

If there were frustrations about his proximity to victory, then they were nothing compared to the plight of Manuel Elvira. Heard of him? If you hadn’t then that would make most of us.

Ranked 296th in the world, and without a win of any description in his eight years as a professional, the Spaniard, 30, had the DP World Tour’s flagship event in the palm of his hands. And then he suffered one of those gut-squeezing chokes that crop up in this maddening game.

His dramas came on the fairway of the 18th hole, a par five, where he stood at 17 under par. His drive had left 228 yards to the front of the green and this hole had been a birdie-fest all week. With Spaun already in the clubhouse, a par would have guaranteed Elvira a play-off; a four would be worth £1.3million and more than the rest of his journeyman career combined.

What followed was somewhat soul destroying. Having made the nervy decision to lay-up short of the creek, Elvira committed the cardinal sin of missing the fairway and finding a bunker. From there, it got so much worse – he flew his recovery to the foot of the 18th grandstand, where his ball nearly hit a group of journalists, and Elvira then proceeded to duff his fourth into another bunker.

On his victory, Spaun said: ‘It means so much. I've kind of blossomed into this player I never thought I could be'

JJ Spaun's wife Melody accompanied his final round with a Jeremy Clarkson mask on a stick

Rory McIroy's second place means he is only just behind Patrick Reed in the Race to Dubai

By the time his ball disappeared below ground, after his seventh stroke, the series of blunders had cost him around £800,000. A cheque of approximately £500,000 for a share of second place with McIlroy, Aaron Rai and Adam Scott is nothing to be sniffed at, but the tears of his wife at greenside told their own story.

His reaction after signing for a 70: ‘Devastated.’

The spoils instead went to a man who admitted he was playing with a ‘chip on my shoulder’. That was Spaun, the 2025 US Open champion who recently incurred the surprise indignity of being left out of the American team for the Presidents Cup.

Channelling his energies on a trip to Surrey, the late-blooming 36-year-old made his point emphatically with this performance – his closing 67 started with a bogey and not a single blemish followed. Finishing with four birdies in his final five holes, he sealed the deal in style.

That it occurred in England was notable for the fact he is besotted with this country. He and his wife regularly spend holidays in the Cotswolds and more recently he has become addicted to watching Clarkson’s Farm on Amazon Prime – his wife Melody accompanied his final round with a Jeremy Clarkson mask on the end of a stick. Each to their own.

On his victory, Spaun said: ‘It means so much. I've kind of blossomed into this player I never thought I could be. England is a place that's dear to my family's heart and the stars kind of aligned this week for me to come out on top.’

Detailing the Clarkson infatuation, Spaun added: ‘We've grown fond of him, along with the English culture. We take holidays in December in the Cotswolds, and we really enjoy his show. I went to his pub, The Farmer's Dog, with the hopes to catch a glimpse of him but he wasn't around.

‘My wife said we would have a surprise guest following us this week if I competed in the tournament and sure enough on Friday morning I saw the face of Jeremy Clarkson and her holding it. Jeremy was there in spirit and I think he brought me good fortune.’

Golf is nothing if not utterly mystifying. In McIlroy’s case, that extends to understanding his swing, which he warned might take five or six months to fix but looked pretty handy here. His tie for second place means he is only marginally behind Patrick Reed in the Race to Dubai standings for the final two months of the season. If McIlroy can pass the American, he will win the order of merit for an eighth time, equalling Colin Montgomerie.

‘I had my chances out there,’ McIlroy said. ‘I putted OK for the most part this week but I missed a lot of putts. I wish I had some of those putts back but I have to be encouraged with where my game is at.

‘I hit the ball really well today and I’m encouraged with the signs. I just have to keep working at it.

‘I have three events until the end of my DP World Tour season. I'm not sure what Patrick's schedule looks like coming up, but I feel like I have enough opportunities. It would be obviously amazing to match Monty's record.’

Sports.title: Only a late stroke of luck spared dismal Man United defeat at struggling Fulham, but it's Sir Jim Ratcliffe - not Michael Carrick - who must take the blame for his club's worsening crisis, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
Only a late stroke of luck spared dismal Man United defeat at struggling Fulham, but it's Sir Jim Ratcliffe - not Michael Carrick - who must take the blame for his club's worsening crisis, writes OLIVER HOLT

There is a pub on Fulham High Street called The Eight Bells.

Paper signs on the windows say that it is reserved for away fans only and on Sunday afternoon, the strains of Manchester United supporters singing in support of their team drifted into the afternoon sunshine before the game.

It is reputed to be Fulham's oldest pub. In fact, there are unsubstantiated claims it is even older than United's back-four. It might have been more appropriate if it was called The Seven Bells, because that is what United got knocked out of them for much of their clash with Alvaro Arbeloa's side at Craven Cottage.

They were outplayed for long periods of the match but escaped with a 1-1 draw after a stroke of luck in the dying minutes brought them a last-gasp equaliser.

They salvaged a little pride but not much. They have five points from their opening five games against Hull City, Ipswich Town, Everton, Manchester City and Fulham.

A season that began with some hopes of them challenging for the title has collapsed into a situation where they are 10 points behind Manchester City before we have even entered the last week of September. Sir Jim Ratcliffe, their minority owner, is an expert on once great things now 'on the slide'. He has added United to his portfolio.

Manchester United are facing more questions than answers after a 1-1 draw away at Fulham

Michael Carrick watched on in dismay as his side looked second best away against Fulham

'It is quite difficult to see how we arrest it,' Sir Jim said of the UK's travails. That sounds like a dispiritingly familiar refrain to United fans.

It is 13 years since they last won the Premier League title and it will be 14 in May. They are too far behind City and Arsenal already to have any chance of ending their drought.

They had some momentum coming into this campaign. Now they have none.

Manager Michael Carrick will get some of the blame for that but this is not his fault. The horror show that is unfolding now is the fault of Sir Jim and his band of hapless executives who masterminded a dreadful summer transfer window that has left United hopelessly adrift of their rivals.

Knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton last week, spurned by the greatest of their young talents, JJ Gabriel, and at war with their own supporters, United had chances and hit the woodwork twice but they looked more predictable and more weary than Fulham.

This was a Fulham, by the way, that were bottom of the table at the start of play but looked more imaginative, more optimistic, more youthful and more coherent than their opponents.

Fulham's point took them above Tottenham Hotspur, who will spend the three weeks of the international break rooted to the foot of the division.

United had spent the first few minutes of the game chasing lengthening shadows. Fulham played the ball about confidently and patiently. They evaded United's half-hearted attempts to press them until a ball was fizzed in to Gonzalo Garcia on the edge of the United box. Garcia snatched at his shot and dragged it wide but it was a chastening start for the visitors.

Lisandro Martinez deflected the ball past a helpless Senne Lammens in the Man United goal

Calvin Bassey wheeled away in celebration after his initial strike eventually led to the first goal

It was a tough watch for Manchester United's travelling fans, who saw a side devoid of energy

When United finally established a foothold in the game, they nearly took the lead. Lisandro Martinez ran on to a loose ball and hit a dipping swerving shot from 25 yards that was destined for the top corner until Bernd Leno launched himself through the air and tipped it wide.

United came close again midway through the half. Matheus Cunha stole the ball away from a Fulham defender as he tried to shepherd it out of play and pulled the ball back for Bruno Fernandes.

Fernandes clipped it towards goal but the ball rolled against the foot of Leno's right-hand post and dribbled away to safety.

United had made the best chances but Fulham had been the better team.

That dynamic shifted after half an hour when Garcia had a golden chance to put Fulham ahead but miskicked in front of goal as he tried to convert Alex Iwobi's cross. Lammens saved well when Sander Berge tried to convert the loose ball.

Then it was the turn of Josh King to go close. King should have been included in Thomas Tuchel's England squad after an outstanding start to this season but was overlooked. Everything about his play in this match showed why he should have been picked.

Fifteen minutes before half-time, he jinked past Luke Shaw with ease and rifled in a shot that Lammens kept out with his right boot.

In the midst of Fulham's missed chances, United hit the woodwork again. Cunha's shot from the edge of the area deflected off a defender and spun up into the air. It was looping over Leno until the goalkeeper got a hand to it and touched it on to the post. United were being outplayed but they were always in the game.

A minute before the break, Marcus Rashford volleyed over from ten yards out. At the other end, King went past Maguire and fell to the ground as Maguire's arm brushed him on his way through.

It was not a foul but nor was it the yellow card that referee Peter Bankes brandished at King.

Matheus Cunha's late deflected strike ensured Manchester United left with something

The second half started slowly but exploded into life just after the hour. Calvin Bassey wrestled the ball away from Cunha on the edge of the United box and unleashed a fierce left-foot drive. Lammens blocked it with his left leg but the ball rebounded to Martinez.

The Argentina defender could not react quickly enough to control it and it bounced off him and back towards goal. Lammens tried to clear it but got his feet in a tangle and deflected it into his own net. Martinez turned away in dismay.

United thought they had equalised minutes later. Bryan Mbeumo curled a shot goalwards and began to wheel away to celebrate before Leno pulled off a magnificent, flying one-handed save that preserved Fulham's lead.

United dominated possession after that but showed little in the way of cutting edge. It took a slice of fortune to drag them level. Fulham held on until two minutes from the end but then Cunha cut in from the left and fired in a shot. Leno had it covered but it deflected off David Affengruber's outstretched foot and bobbled apologetically over the line.

Sports.title: Furious Jose Mourinho brings PRINTOUTS of referee 'errors' to tense Madrid derby press conference - and blasts 'poor' officials who 'couldn't handle the pressure' after his side's 2-1 defeat
Sports.content:
Furious Jose Mourinho brings PRINTOUTS of referee 'errors' to tense Madrid derby press conference - and blasts 'poor' officials who 'couldn't handle the pressure' after his side's 2-1 defeat

A furious Jose Mourinho lashed out at referee Ortiz Arias, claiming he was not qualified to officiate Sunday's Madrid derby.

Mourinho ended up on the losing side as his 10-man Real Madrid lost 2-1 at the Wanda Metropolitano against fierce city rivals Atletico Madrid.

Still seething in the press conference, Mourinho arrived with printed out photos which showed, in his opinion, a series of major calls missed by the referee.

'We could save ourselves the press conference,' an irritated Mourinho began.

'Here they are [shows photos of the possible red cards], two clear reds. It would have been 50 minutes of 11 against nine. All I can do is hug my players, who gave everything, who produced a first half full of class and personality. I prepared the match so we could win it in the second half.'

Rather than pick apart the performance of his players, which saw Dean Huijsen sent off, he focused in on the 'poor' performance of Arias, a referee he does not believe is suitable for the biggest games.

Jose Mourinho was furious at the refereeing performance of Ortiz Arias (right) on Sunday

Mourinho was so livid at the refereeing performance he printed out fouls he felt were missed

'The one who should be happy is the Refereeing Appointments Committee because the whole thing was very strange,' Mourinho's rant continued.

'A week in advance, they already knew who the referee would be, when it used to be 24 hours before. A 41-year-old referee, who has never been an international, that won't be top level.

'The poor guy came here and couldn't handle the pressure.

'The pressure here is like something out of the 1980s. Trujillo, the VAR official, called him over for the first red and didn't call him over for the second, which was even clearer. This Trujillo has a history with Real Madrid: last year in the Copa final, Osasuna, Girona...

'If the poor referee has no experience, no stature for a derby, then this man is either under no pressure, or under a kind of pressure we know nothing about.

'I would have liked to leave here with the win or without having to speak. I arrived here three months ago and you know I'm not usually one to go in this direction.

'Two reds against Elche and we won. Two reds today, that's already more difficult. It's a referee with only small matches behind him and a VAR official who has a history.

'Congratulations to the Refereeing Appointments Committee.'

Mourinho was in disbelief at a referee he is adamant will never make it to the highest level

Mourinho is an expert at making his point in press conferences and this was one of his finest since returning to Spain.

Goals from Grimaldo, who scored from the penalty spot, and Jonathan David ensured Diego Simeone's side won it 2-1. Antonio Rudiger's late goal was merely a consolation.

But it was the fact that Atletico Madrid kept all 11 players on the pitch en route to victory that most irked Mourinho and Madrid.

Mourinho's print-outs included one tackle by Cristian Romero on Bellingham, which looked particularly bad upon second viewing but only drew a yellow card.

Kang-In Lee's tackle on Fede Valverde went without punishment, while Huijsen got a straight red card for holding Giuliano Simeone inside the box.

In an official club statement, Real Madrid said: 'Real Madrid lose the derby at the Metropolitano in a match marked by Ortiz Arias' VERY TERRIBLE REFEREEING.

'He failed to send off Cuti Romero in the first half for stepping on Bellingham's knee (despite going to the monitor to review the incident), nor did he send off Kang-In Lee for stepping on Valverde's left ankle.

'Both decisions had an impact on the match, which was ultimately decided in Atlético's favor in the second half.'

🚨🫵🏽 Jude Bellingham against the referee at full time: “Two red cards! Two!”.@postunited — oscarolleroo on IG 📸 pic.twitter.com/1qkCTlsMUO — Fabrizio Romano (@FabrizioRomano) September 20, 2026

Real Madrid's Jude Bellingham was furious at officials after Cristian Romero was not sent off

Frustration in Real Madrid's ranks also extended to star man Jude Bellingham who was seen giving the referee a piece of his mind following the final whistle.

Footage showed the Englishman shouting 'oh my god' at Arias, before adding 'two red cards!'

Bellingham was particularly aggrieved that Romero's challenge on him did not see red when replays suggested that it was a sending off offence.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick denies Gary Neville claim in staunch defence of Man Utd stars
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick denies Gary Neville claim in staunch defence of Man Utd stars

Manchester United have endured a poor start to Michael Carrick's first full season at the helm but the Red Devils boss has come out fighting with his assessment of his side's performance

View 2 Images Michael Carrick's Manchester United have endured a poor start to the season (Image: Getty Images)

Michael Carrick insisted Manchester United can still have a “big season” after Gary Neville branded the performance “absolutely pathetic.”

‌



Matheus Cunha’s deflected shot snatched a last-minute draw but the result drew stinging criticism from Sky pundit Neville as United go into the international break languishing in 12th place.

‌



Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa, whose side gained a point to leave Tottenham rock bottom, could also find himself trouble with the FA after claiming refs “don’t like Manchester United to lose” as he was upset with some of Peter Bankes’ decisions.

‌



Neville was very critical on Sky about the way United played at the start of the second half and said: “I've watched Man United since the age of five. That's the worst 15 minutes I've seen them play. Absolutely pathetic.”

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



But Carrick, whose side are already ten points behind leaders Manchester City, said: “There’s still a big season ahead. It’s a long season and this is part of the journey.

“I’m not playing it down - we wanted more points. I understand the frustration. But what bothers me is that we want better results.

“We want more points, we're going to have a spell where it's not quite going for you and we've had a spell of that where small things have ended up as big things.

‌



“We don't think things are perfect by any means. We need to win football matches. The supporters were top-drawer again today and we have to give them something to keep shouting about.

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has given his verdict on Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

“I think we did enough to win the game. I think we could win it. I was pleased with how we responded, the boys kept their belief and kept doing the right things. I think a point is the least we should take.”

‌



Carrick was also asked about Neville's comments and if his side were 'too passive' at Craven Cottage but claimed that he did not share that verdict.

He said: "I didn't think we were. Did you think we were? Football is a difficult game. We controlled a lot of the first half. It's the Premier League and you will have spells where you don't have it all your own way. To expect total dominance for the whole game, I don't think anyone gets that in this league."

He added: "I think we can take a lot from today. I think we can learn a lot as well. We can be better at certain things, that is pretty clear, but there were some god signs today."

Sports.title: Premier League propose big Carabao Cup change in £1.8bn 'new deal for football'
Sports.content:
Premier League propose big Carabao Cup change in £1.8bn 'new deal for football'

The Premier League are offering the English Football League a 'new deal for football' worth £1.8billion, but they now want one massive change to the Carabao Cup

View 2 Images Premier League clubs wants changes to the Carabao Cup semi-finals (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

The Premier League reportedly want Carabao Cup semi-final ties to be decided over one match rather than two as part of a 'new deal for football'. A proposed agreement with the English Football League is said to effectively double the existing solidarity payment, which is divided among clubs across all three EFL divisions, to £1.8billion.

‌



It would be spread across 10 seasons, and both leagues are reportedly around £27million apart in negotiations. However, there is growing confidence of an agreement.

‌



Premier League clubs have unanimously approved the proposal. EFL sides doing likewise would avoid any involvement by the Independent Football Regulator (IFR).

‌



Andros Townsend delivers perfect response after being run over by pitch roller in freak accident READ MORE :

Richarlison takes to social media with clear message after Tottenham lose again READ MORE :

The Daily Mail reports that another condition of their additional funding would be to progress talks with the National League over new clubs earning League Two promotion every season. They cite sources that claim the Premier League wants to reduce its reliance on ownership funding for EFL clubs.

Controls on how these funds are spent are proposed, including a stop on any increases in player wages. The proposition also requires 15% of the funds to go towards infrastructure.

It also features a 'lifeboat fund' for clubs entering administration in future. They would be loaned £20million to continue paying essential creditors and operating.

‌



View 2 Images The Carabao Cup semi-finals could stopping being two-legged ties (Image: Paul Currie/Shutterstock)

The EFL want a tweak to their current divisional split of 80:12:8 between the Championship, League One and League Two. Despite the Premier League seeking no change, a change to 75:15:10 is being sought.

Under the new split, based on a mid-table finish, Championship clubs would receive £8.5million more, rising from £12.1million to £20.6million. That translates to a £1.3million uplift in League One, up from £2.5million to £3.8million, whereas League Two payments would grow by £700k, from £1.8million to £2.5million. A 2% increase in the Premier League transfer levy is to cover the increase, which would go from 4% to 6%.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The deal is around 17.5% of what all top-flight clubs earn from their collective broadcast rights. That is 6.5% more than the current level, but half of what the EFL initially sought.

EFL clubs were told about the proposal last week. They will make the final decision once it is ready for the league's board to recommend.

Article continues below

The deal has already been under discussion for six weeks now. It is said that the EFL prefers to wait until the IFR's State of the Game report, which is due to be published by them on 12 October.

Sports.title: JJ Gabriel 'chooses Chelsea' transfer after Man Utd exit bombshell
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel 'chooses Chelsea' transfer after Man Utd exit bombshell

News that JJ Gabriel wants to depart Manchester United sent shockwaves through the Premier League, but one report is now claiming he has chosen a new club

View 3 Images JJ Gabriel recently told Manchester United he wants to leave (Image: 2026 Manchester United FC)

Manchester United teenager JJ Gabriel has reportedly decided he wants to move to Chelsea. The 15-year-old prodigy has formally requested to be de-registered by the Reds, which would essentially make him a free agent.

‌



His demand blind-sided Michael Carrick's side, particularly after he was expected to be in the squad for United's 3-2 defeat to Brighton and Hove Albion in the League Cup. Gabriel recently travelled to Barcelona, who outlined their vision for youngster.

‌



Real Madrid have also been linked with Gabriel, who would be able to play in Spain despite being 15 due to the fact he has an Irish EU passport. If he was to stay in England, it's been claimed Chelsea are the club he would choose, although the Blues would have to wait until January 2027, due to the fact they were banned from registering new academy players for nine months in March.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

TEAMtalk have stated that out of every English club to reach out to him, the Blues' pitch was the most attractive. Gabriel is yet to sign a scholarship agreement with United.

Young player are forbidden from signing a scholarship agreement until they turn 16 years old, which Gabriel will do on October 6. If he was to move to Spain, United would be due a small windfall.

‌



This is due to rules allowing a 16-year-old with an EU passport to move to a team within the European Union. United would be entitled to a compensation payment, which is set by a tariff based on the number of years the player has spent at a club.

View 3 Images Gabriel is being eyed by many of Europe's top clubs (Image: 2026 Manchester United FC)

There have been examples of this happening in the past, when Arsenal signed Cesc Fabregas when he was a teenager as well as United bringing Gerard Pique to the club. However, it would be substantially less than the amount due if he joined an English club - a recent example of which was Rio Ngumoha's move from Chelsea to Liverpool, which cost a minimum of £2.8million.

‌



Carrick has called for calm when asked about the situation around the prodigy, reminding the football world he is still only a child. The United manager said: "I think I’d just repeat what I said the other day, really.

"I think he’s a young boy, JJ, and I think it’s important that we certainly don’t put anything out here. I think the exposure and the scrutiny and everything that, you got to be careful and be sensible and think of him as much as anything.

View 3 Images Gabriel was not included in any England youth squads for this international break (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

"The situation will work itself out, whatever way it’s going to work itself out. Making sure he’s okay is the important thing.”

Gabriel was dropped by all of the England youth teams amid the transfer saga this week. He missed out on a place with the under-19s and under-17s for the coming international break.

Sports.title: Referees attacked by rugby fans as security rushes to shield them from projectiles
Sports.content:
Referees attacked by rugby fans as security rushes to shield them from projectiles

Newcastle Knights secured a dramatic victory over the New Zealand Warriors in the NRL semi-final but the controversial win saw the officials have to take shelter as they were barraged by projectiles

View 2 Images The match ended in ugly scenes (Image: X: @centralNRL)

Furious spectators launched projectiles at the match officials following the final whistle of a major National Rugby League clash in New Zealand. Referee Ashley Klein and his team had to take cover as bottles were launched in their direction by angry fans after Newcastle Knights pulled off a stunning upset against New Zealand Warriors.

‌



The Knights claimed a 12-10 win at Auckland's Eden Park, but the result did not come without controversy as the visitors booked their place in the NRL's preliminary finals for the first time since 2013. Two pivotal decisions went against the Warriors in the dying moments, much to the frustration of those in the stands.

‌



In the 79th minute, Warriors centre Leka Halasima was felled off the ball by Knights prop Tyson Frizell as he prepared to challenge for a high kick. The crowd were expecting a penalty that would allow the Warriors to level the scores in the final seconds and send the game to a 'Golden Point'.

‌



Despite replays appearing to show fairly conclusive evidence, Klein sensationally waved away the incident, leaving a record crowd of 48,500 seeing red. That decision followed bunker official Chris Butler declining to overturn a call as Warriors' Te Maire Martin was penalised for a strip that may have been a loose carry.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Butler had moments earlier reversed a Knights knock-on. The divisive ending to the fixture resulted in Klein and his match officials being met with a cacophony of boos and jeers as they left Eden Park.

‌



But they could not escape without fans launching cans and bottles towards them as they attempted to make their way into the depths of the stadium.

Security staff and stewards were compelled to step in to shield the refereeing squad from flying objects, as the officials covered their heads and beat a swift retreat down the tunnel.

View 2 Images Newcastle Knights upset the New Zealand Warriors (Image: Hannah Peters, Getty Images)

‌



When the match concluded, Warriors boss Andrew Webster acknowledged that the eleventh-hour decisions that counted against his outfit were "frustrating", but insisted they weren't the deciding factor in his team's loss.

"It was frustrating," he said. "I feel like they were trying to find ways to take it off us.

"The last one, and two points would have drawn the game, he's [Frizell] going across Leka, pretending to try and catch the ball, which they [NRL] have told us you can't do."

Article continues below

Knights boss Justin Holbrook had no issues, however. “I thought they were all right,” he said post-match.

“I thought he stripped it with his hand and ripped it like that,” he offered when asked about the strip.

The Knights will now progress to take on Penrith in the preliminary final at Sydney's Accor Stadium next weekend.

Sports.title: Matheus Cunha makes worrying Man Utd admission after Fulham draw - 'We cannot accept this'
Sports.content:
Matheus Cunha makes worrying Man Utd admission after Fulham draw - 'We cannot accept this'

Manchester United's inconsistent start to the season continued against Fulham on Sunday evening with Matheus Cunha popping up late on to salvage a draw at Craven Cottage

View 2 Images Matheus Cunha speaks after Man Utd's draw with Fulham

Matheus Cunha slammed his Manchester United teammates for not working as hard as Fulham in their draw at Craven Cottage. The Red Devils looked to be on their way to another defeat on Sunday afternoon after Lisandro Martinez had put through his own net.

‌



Brazilian forward Cunha popped up late on the steal a late draw, albeit it leaves United with just five points from their opening five games of the season - their joint-worst start to a Premier League campaign ever.

‌



Giving his assessment, Cunha claimed that United were outworked by their hosts. Speaking to Sky Sports, he said: “So frustrating for us because I feel like in the beginning we put the ball in and created some chances.

‌



"We didn’t score, unlucky, and they scored in like one action that’s hard to explain. A lot of luck. Then you come back and this is frustrating because I feel to be honest after we conceding the goal we played much better with a lot of enthusiasm and effort. It’s only one point. We try to never play for one point.”

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



He added: “It’s hard to explain. I feel like after the first half we played well. It was how we planned to do it in the beginning of the second half. I feel like they put more into it than us and we cannot accept this. We always play better after conceding a goal but it cannot be like this."

Asked what has to change to get the side back on track, Cunha said: “I have to be honest today I don’t feel like it was about the final decision. We were a bit unlucky. I hit the post. Bruno hit the post. We had other chances. We need to create more and then it will come to us and then we will score more goals.

"Everything we can do to help the team, it's acceptable. When I have the ball, it is not that much difference. Of course we need to improve in every single position. If there is something I can do to help, I will do it."

‌



View 2 Images Cunha scored late on at Craven Cottage (Image: Getty Images)

United's draw at Craven Cottage leaves them with just one win and in 12th in the Premier League. Despite being left frustrated, Cunha has assured that there is still plenty of time for the side to turn things around.

He said: "To be honest, I don't think about outside. I always try to help my teammates. I feel very priviliged to play in this role. It is only the beginning. Last season, there was a lot of noise about and we finished third."

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn reveals Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury 'drug testing' delay before announcement
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn reveals Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury 'drug testing' delay before announcement

Eddie Hearn has provided an update on Anthony Joshua's expected bout against Tyson Fury later this year suggesting a date is 'locked in' but another issue has cropped up

View Image Eddie Hearn has provided an update on Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury (Image: Ben Roberts Photo/Getty Images)

Eddie Hearn has revealed another problem ahead of Anthony Joshua's anticipated bout with Tyson Fury. The British boxing giants finally looked to be on a collision course later this year, before a dispute over the destination of the fight.

‌



Plans appeared to be being put in place for a monumental clash at Madison Square Garden in New York on November 20, AJ's contract for the fight includes a clause insisting it takes place in the United Kingdom. His determination to see that honoured has seen Cardiff's Principality Stadium come into the running, though the bout could be pushed back until December.

‌



But the location of the fight is not the only area causing some contract confusion, according to Hearn. The boxing promoter has suggested there is a discrepancy in expectations between Joshua and Fury.

‌



Olympic champion Joshua has already been required to undergo drug testing since the outset of the bout agreement, while Hearn isn't convinced the same stipulation is within Fury's agreement.

Conor Benn has world title shot shut down just days after Ryan Garcia loss READ MORE :

"The drug testing protocol was the same as what has always been in there," said Hearn, following Pat Brown's win over John Hedges on Saturday. "It wasn't adhered to in its form.

"I don't actually necessarily blame Tyson Fury for that. As we've found out on many occasions, what's in AJ's contract is not necessarily in Tyson Fury's contract.

‌



"Testing was supposed to start when the original contracts were signed, and it didn't for them. And I don't think [Fury] had in his contract that it had to start then.

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

"So this is not me saying, 'He didn't enrol'. I don't think he was obligated to enrol [in his contract]. But in our contract, he was obligated to enrol. There have been many issues along the way with the contract that we have let slip and ride because we want to stay in the fight and make sure it happens."

‌



Despite that, Hearn believes that a date for the fight is now locked and that announcement is imminent. Regular conversations have taken place with Netflix.

He said: "Over the last week or two, obviously we made our decision, and AJ was the guy leading that decision that we weren’t interested in accepting any extra money or changing the terms of the agreement to change the location.

"He decided that he wanted to make sure that the fight was in the UK, and since then they've accepted that. We've worked together and we've been speaking to Netflix on regular occasions to basically lock in the date.

Article continues below

"I think the date is locked in, and I'll let them give you the official announcement. It was supposed to be this week, but I think it's going to be very, very soon."

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola launches Florian Wirtz defence after stinging Jamie Carragher criticism
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola launches Florian Wirtz defence after stinging Jamie Carragher criticism

Jamie Carragher was critical of Florian Wirtz's performance against Bournemouth, but Andoni Iraola reckons that he made the difference for Liverpool in the second half

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola was left pleased with Florian Wirtz (Image: aspafotos/MB Media/Getty Images)

Andoni Iraola has praised Florian Wirtz for his second-half turnaround which helped Liverpool beat Bournemouth 1-0. The Reds claimed all three points at the Vitality Stadium, with Alexander Isak scoring the decisive goal.

‌



But it wasn't going Liverpool's way in the first half, with Wirtz in particular struggling to have a positive impact on the game. That was when Jamie Carragher singled out the £116million signing, saying: "Wirtz has been really poor again. It's just nothing. Nothing is happening there at all.

‌



"In the main, people have been understanding of his situation. He's new to the league and Liverpool were poor last season. When you come for that price tag, people want goals and assists."

‌



In the second period, the 23-year-old was more lively and played a part in Isak's goal, drawing James Hill out to give his team-mate space to finish. But when Wirtz was subbed off in the 73rd minute, Carragher brutally said that he could have 'no complaints'.

‌



Iraola, though, believes that the German ultimately helped Liverpool win the match, telling Sky Sports: "He started the game slowly, I agree. The first minute they went quite intense and we were not quite with us.

"The duels in the middle. After that first phase, I think we improved. Florian has helped us also to improve.

"Second half he was playing much better, he was finding better spots to receive and turn. Probably we haven't found the last part or moment to score but I think I'm much more happy with his second half than his first one."

‌

View 3 Images Florian Wirtz was criticised by Jamie Carragher against Bournemouth (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Iraola added: "I'm obviously happy with the result. I know it's a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points.

‌



"We could see in the game, at the beginning in the first 20 minutes, we weren't at the level at the game, and it has cost us until afterwards, where we finished the first half better.

"The second half we played better. But that beginning of the game kind of - not surprised us because we knew where we were coming to - but it was difficult for us.

View 3 Images Jamie Carragher branded Florian Wirtz 'really poor' in the first half (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Article continues below

"We could see a bit later when Bournemouth started to get tired that in the second half we controlled the game much better. We even had chances to finish but didn't score the second one. But that first part of the game, we were not winning duels, second balls and when they play with this intensity, you have to be at their level."
