World.title: Croatian Military Special Forces Take 1st Place at FPV Drone Pilots Competition
World.content:
September the 20th, 2026 – Croatian military special forces have won 1st place at an international FPV drone pilots competition.

Members of the Croatian Special Forces Command of the Armed Forces recently won first place at the international military competition for FPV drone pilots in the TACTICAL category. Morski reports that this win means they have achieved an outstanding result in competition with international military teams.

The competition was held from the 13th to the 18th of September at the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst in the UK. Called the international military competition for FPV drone pilots “British Army Tactical Drone Competition – BADCT and Military International Drone Racing Tournament – MIDRT”, the Croatian team certainly wowed. Croatia was represented at the competition by members of the Special Forces Command of the Croatian Armed Forces who, thanks to an exceptional level of training, professionalism and teamwork, won first place in the TACTICAL category. Second place was taken by Ukraine, while Germany came third.

an extremely demanding competition

The competition brought together more than 80 competitors, members of the armed forces from several countries, and during the multi-day programme the participants demonstrated a high level of knowledge and skills in controlling FPV drones. In the first part of the competition, a contest in the tactical use of drones was held, which included an obstacle course, dropping a bomb with a drone and intercepting another aircraft in the air, in which the members of the Special Forces Command achieved an enviable result in an international military environment. The continuation of the competition included FPV drone races.

In addition to Croatia, Ukraine and Germany, representatives of Australia, Australian cadets, the United States of America, the United Kingdom, American veterans, New Zealand, Sweden and France also took part in the competition. This result represents significant recognition for the members of the Special Forces Command of the Croatian Armed Forces and confirms their knowledge, skills and ability to apply modern technology in a demanding international environment.

World.title: If Government Fails to Intervene, Croatia’s Most Expensive Diesel is Coming
World.content:
September the 19th, 2026 – If the government fails to intervene, then Croatia’s most expensive diesel so far is on its way next week.

From next Tuesday, drivers at petrol stations could be met with higher fuel prices. Index reports that according to what currently remains unofficial information, all types of fuel are becoming more expensive, and diesel could reach a historic high in Croatia. These are the prices that will apply if the government fails to properly intervene, reports RTL.

expected price increases

If there is no government intervention, the price of a litre of eurosuper should rise by one cent and amount to €1.74. Eurodiesel would become more expensive by ten cents, so its new price would be €1.95 per litre. The largest price increase is expected for blue diesel, which should rise by 11 cents to €1.51.

historic highs for diesel…

If the government does not make a different decision, the diesel price of €1.95 per litre would be the highest recorded in Croatia’s history. Until now Croatia has had some of the lower fuel prices in Europe, but that could change from next week.

why are diesel and oil prices rising like this?

The background to the new blow to drivers’ pockets lies in the global disruptions caused by the US war against Iran, which has been shaking the world energy market for months. The situation escalated further after drone attacks on the Saudi East-West oil pipeline, a key alternative route for transporting crude oil after navigation through the Strait of Hormuz became unsafe. As a result, Brent crude prices jumped above $100 a barrel, and some deliveries in Europe exceeded $120.

As energy expert Davor Štern warned, the price increases are not only a consequence of a physical shortage of fuel, but primarily of stock-market speculation. “We follow the markets, and the markets do what they do. The exchanges have again returned to their traditional bookmaking methods – it is not so much a real shortage of diesel as expectations that there will not be enough of it that have driven the price up,” Štern explained.

the croatian government’s hands are tied…

On whether the state even has mechanisms with which it could stop this rise, Professor Marijana Ivanov from the Department of Finance at the Faculty of Economics in Zagreb spoke for Index. She warns that the geopolitical circumstances are extremely unfavourable and that the Government is running out of instruments with which it could cushion new blows.

“I think the room for preventing a further rise in fuel prices is quite limited. With excise duties there is almost none, especially with diesel, while with petrol it is also very narrow,” Ivanov points out. Although cutting the VAT rate is often mentioned in public, the economist considers that this would not be a good move: “In principle it is possible to reduce VAT on fuel, but I would not suggest it because public finances are already under pressure from the risk of a larger deficit. A third option would be further cutting of distributors’ margins, but we know that even at these levels they have become unsustainable for small traders.”

World.title: Will Croatia Have Enough Energy Capacities to Match Consumption Growth?
World.content:
September the 19th, 2026 – Will Croatia have enough energy capacities for both the general public and for the economy as consumption increases?

Experts keep on emphasising that without a stronger electricity grid and larger energy storage capacities it will not be possible to keep up with the growth in consumption. The question in many minds now is whether or not Croatia will have enough energy capacities for the economy, the public and new industry, and at competitive prices? Poslovni reports that this was one of the key questions at the ENERGREEN – Energy Security of Croatia 2027 conference.

The focus was primarily placed on the security of gas supply, the LNG terminal on Krk and the Okoli storage facility, as well as the accelerated development of solar and wind power plants, as reported by HRT. Experts emphasise that without a stronger electricity grid and larger energy storage capacities it will not be possible to keep up with the growth in consumption. When it comes to heating, people have no reason to worry. “Croatia has a relatively good energy situation due to its geostrategic position, and the country is home to an LNG terminal, storage, and good transport infrastructure, which means that we will always have enough gas, because now we’re no longer last in line but first,” explained Dalibor Pudić, president of the Croatian Professional Gas Association.

“As you’ve already seen, the 11th package of measures has also been adopted. The government is very much continuing to protect the general public and the concrete economy; in addition, there is also supply stability through certain measures, limiting retail fuel prices, and supply stability is also ensured through the filling of gas storage facilities,” concluded Željko Krevzelj, director of the Energy Directorate at the Ministry of the Economy.

World.title: Renovated University Campus Worth Over €50 Million Opens in Zagreb
World.content:
September the 19th, 2026 – A newly renovated university campus worth over €50 million has opened as part of FER in Zagreb.

After two years of extensive works, Buildings B and C of the campus of the Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computing of the University of Zagreb (FER) were solemnly opened. The complete renovation amounting to €50 million excluding VAT was co-financed with European Union funds from the Solidarity Fund and the Recovery and Resilience Facility. Poslovni reports that this concerns an area spanning 18,000 square metres in Unska Street that includes five modern amphitheatre lecture halls with a capacity of 900 seats, 153 office rooms and 26 classrooms and laboratories for teaching. The newly opened FER premises were visited by representatives of the state leadership, the City of Zagreb, the University of Zagreb and prominent entrepreneurs, members of the Faculty’s Alumni Board.

FER Dean Prof. Vedran Bilas, PhD, said that the investment in the renovation is the initial phase of the campus development, which was last expanded at the end of the 1980s, when the faculty had almost half as many employees, fewer study programmes and many times fewer research projects than today.

“Generations of professors and students before us built this institution, its competences, significance and values. FER is a synonym of excellence in the Croatian public, academic and business community. This renovation and this ceremony are stations on a path that continues. The Faculty has an experienced and proven team and capacity for the implementation of complex infrastructure projects, ready to continue cooperation with the Ministry of Science, Education and Youth on campus development projects,” Bilas said and announced a new spatial expansion: “The Government of the Republic of Croatia, through a Loan Agreement with the World Bank, is financing the preparation of the main project for the reconstruction of Building A, which will be completed by the end of this year. The reconstructed building will have three underground and nine above-ground floors, five more than now.”

Prime Minister Andrej Plenković praised the Faculty’s results and emphasised its contribution to society.

“By renovating these buildings we aren’t investing merely in space, but in Croatia’s ability to understand, shape and lead the technological changes that in the decades ahead will determine the economic strength, security and technological independence of states. FER is one of the central places where Croatia creates knowledge for the digital age, and we count on its professors, researchers and students also in responding to the challenges of artificial intelligence, cyber security and quantum computing. Our vision is clear: Croatia must not be only a user of other people’s technology, but must develop and export its own high value-added solutions,” said Prime Minister Plenković.

“Through patient work, persistence and joint action we have arrived at a result that benefits our teachers and those most important for our future, and that is our students. I believe that the Faculty in the renovated premises will develop new visions and continue to lead in the IT sector and digital transformation, recognising what society and the state need,” said Rector of the University of Zagreb, Prof. Stjepan Lakušić, PhD.

The FER team responsible for the implementation of the renovation guided representatives of the Government, Prime Minister Plenković, Minister of Construction and State Property Branko Bačić, Minister of the Economy Ante Šušnjar and other high-ranking guests through the newly renovated premises, and the tour ended on the 13th floor with a spectacular panoramic view of the whole of Zagreb. The contractor for the extensive works was the construction company TROMONT d.o.o., and a complete energy, fire-protection and multimedia renovation was carried out.

The programme and celebration of the opening will continue in the afternoon. From 18:00 a parking party for friends, fellow citizens and neighbours is planned on the FER car park in Unska Street, with musicians Duška Brčić, Vjeko Ključarić, Filip Rudan, young up-and-coming bands and the Disco section of KSET.

World.title: “Forever Chemicals” Found in Lika Water Following Waste Scandal
World.content:
September the 19th, 2026 – So-called “forever chemicals” have unfortunately been found in Lika water following the shameful hazardous waste scandal.

The Croatian Institute of Public Health (HZJZ) and the Public Health Institute of Lika-Senj County have published the results of extraordinary water sampling in the Lika area. Index reports that the results have revealed that dangerous PFAS compounds, so-called “forever chemicals,” were found in two private wells downstream from an illegal waste dump near Gospić, but they assure the public that the pollution is exclusively of a local character and that water from the public water supply is not endangered.

the chemicals were found in two wells near the illegal waste dump

According to the HZJZ statement, from the 20th of August to the 9th of September water was sampled from 43 private facilities – 38 wells, three cisterns and two springs. The Institute states that in one well in the immediate vicinity of the dump a concentration of PFAS compounds of 0.3018 µg/L was recorded, which is three times higher than the maximum permitted limit of 0.1 µg/L. In the second well 0.0265 µg/L was measured, which is within the permitted limits. HZJZ claims that the owners of the disputed wells are connected to the public water supply and do not use that water for drinking. As for the other findings, the Institute claims that in 33 facilities only “usual microbiological pollution characteristic of untreated water” was recorded, while elevated physical-chemical values in a further 10 samples are attributed to the natural properties of the karst, and not to the dumped waste.

the people of lika feel betrayed by the government

The statement comes at a moment when the scandal surrounding the illegal burial of as many as 37,000 tonnes of hazardous waste in Divoselo and Benkovačko Selo near Gospić has grown into a first-class political scandal. HZJZ Director Krunoslav Capak personally sits on the newly established Scientific Council of Prime Minister Andrej Plenković, a body that the government formed precisely with the aim of “correctly interpreting” in public the dramatic findings of the USKOK investigation into the pollution of soil and waters in Lika. The documents that Plenković’s Scientific Council is supposed to put into the “correct context” were signed by authorised institutions and are quite exact.

The expert examination by the “Josip Juraj Strossmayer” Water Institute for the Divoselo location established that the water passing immediately under the dump carries 89 percent of the total detected plastic, while upstream it is clean. 737 micrograms of Styrofoam per litre were measured, and the presence of Teflon from the group of “forever chemicals” (PFAS) was also recorded, with the expert’s note that the Lika River is a directly connected water body.

the prime minister is at the council’s helm

Although formally composed of professors from technical and natural science faculties, the Council has been placed under the direct authority of the Prime Minister. According to the government decision, the sessions are convened and chaired by Plenković himself, operational tasks are carried out by his office, and there are no prescribed obligations for the publication of minutes, expert conclusions or any dissenting opinions of members. The entire manoeuvre of forming the Council is taking place at a time when the remediation is only being prepared, and political pressure on the ruling party is growing after a mass protest in Zagreb and a drop in HDZ’s rating.

is there any real reason to panic?

Despite this, HZJZ persists in the claim that there is no reason for panic. They state that the fact that such compounds were not found in other wells across the county proves that it is “pollution of a local character in a narrower circle.” They also repeat that private wells in any case do not fall under regular state supervision and that the responsibility lies with the owners themselves. The Institute finally states that all regular tests confirm that water from the public water supply in the entire Lika-Senj County area, as well as on the islands of Pag and Rab, is completely health-safe and that they will continue monitoring the situation on the ground.

World.title: Iraq confirms foreign reserves enough to meet demand
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) confirmed on Saturday that its foreign currency reserves are entirely sufficient to meet all market demands.

The step aims to counter a wave of market instability and a surging US currency in the parallel exchange markets.

The CBI indicated that current reserves are sufficient to finance foreign commerce, bank card transactions, and travelers’ cash requests at the official rate of 1,320 dinars per US dollar.

The bank stated that reports of increased exchange rates and sluggish market activity did not indicate a scarcity of hard cash.

The bank blamed the rising parallel market gap, where the US dollar soared beyond 1,600 Iraqi dinars, on speculation, manipulation, and the exploitation of regional geopolitical concerns rather than any true dollar shortage.

The announcement comes as figures show Iraq’s foreign reserves decreased to $80.63 billion at the end of July. Financial experts say that these reserves are still within extremely safe boundaries, capable of supporting more than nine months of national imports.

The CBI has asked individuals to depend solely on official statements and data and to lodge any complaints or queries directly through the CBI complaint portal.

World.title: Iraq’s foreign reserves decline to $80.6 billion in July
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Figures released by the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) showed that the country’s foreign reserves declined to $80.63 billion at the end of July 2026, compared to $86.17 billion at the end of June and $97.432 billion at the end of 2025.

Foreign reserves in US dollars fell by roughly $16.79 billion in the first seven months of 2026 compared to the end of 2025, representing a reduction of nearly 17.2 percent.

The value of foreign reserves in Iraqi dinars declined to 104.82 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $80.19 billion) at the end of July, compared to 112.02 trillion Iraqi dinars (about $85.7 billion) at the end of June and 126.66 trillion Iraqi dinars (nearly $96.9 billion) at the end of 2025.

The value of gold reserves saw a slight increase to 29.66 trillion Iraqi dinars (nearly $22.7 billion) at the end of July, compared to 29.41 trillion Iraqi dinars (about $22.5 billion) at the end of June, but remained below their level at the end of 2025, which was 31.48 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $24.08 billion).

The CBI’s investments declined to 75.03 trillion Iraqi dinars (about $57.4 billion) at the end of July, compared to 81.99 trillion Iraqi dinars (around $62.7 billion) at the end of June and 93.26 trillion Iraqi dinars ($71.34 billion) at the end of 2025.

Cash reserves held in the CBI’s vaults also decreased to 124 billion Iraqi dinars ($94.86 million) at the end of July, compared to 614 billion Iraqi dinars (nearly $470 million) at the end of June and 1.9 trillion Iraqi dinars ($1.45 billion) at the end of 2025.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports hit three million barrels in September
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s oil exports fluctuated during September 2026, amid ongoing geopolitical tensions related to the Middle East war and Baghdad’s efforts to diversify its export routes.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told Attaqa News that exports started at three million barrels per day at the beginning of September but have since gradually declined to about 2.4 million barrels per day at present.

Despite a decline in Iraqi oil exports during September, the figures still surpassed the average daily exports in August, which were approximately 2.35 million barrels per day. This increase was bolstered by enhanced shipping traffic and a decrease in shipping disruptions in the Gulf over the past few weeks.

Data indicates that Iraq’s oil exports continue to be affected by the repercussions of the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz, despite improved export routes in the past few weeks. Baghdad is working to secure alternatives and enhance the operational capacity of its oil terminals.

Despite a relative improvement, Iraq’s current oil exports remain below pre-February 2026 levels, reflecting continued pressure on supply chains, after shipments reached approximately 73 million barrels in August, according to data released by Iraq’s State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO).

The average daily export volume of Iraqi oil in August 2026 surged to approximately 2.354 million barrels. This figure represents a significant increase compared to the combined total of roughly 526,470 barrels per day in May and June. This rise marks the highest levels of oil export and revenue since the onset of the US-Israeli war against Iran.

Iraq’s oil exports during August were distributed between the country’s southern maritime terminals and the Turkish port of Ceyhan via the northern outlet.

The increase in exports comes amid an easing of shipping delays in the Arabian Gulf and Iran’s authorization for certain oil tankers transporting Iraqi oil to traverse the Strait of Hormuz.

Iraq’s oil exports indicate a notable recovery compared to previous months, with revenues reaching approximately $4.5 billion in August, compared to $2.336 billion in May and June combined.

World.title: Six French ISIS suspects face trial in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – An Iraqi court launched on Sunday the trial of six French nationals suspected of membership in the terrorist group ISIS.

A member of the Supreme Judicial Council warned that the suspects might face the death sentence if convicted of crimes against Iraq and its people.

According to two court legal sources, the defendants were among 47 French ISIS inmates relocated from prisons in northeast Syria in 2025 as part of an operation authorized by US forces and Iraqi officials.

According to Reuters, officials from the French embassy in Iraq were present at the Baghdad criminal court.

The six inmates being tried under Iraq’s counter-terrorism law arrived in the court in a prison van accompanied by a convoy of Humvees carrying Iraqi Special Forces officers.

The suspects were wearing yellow prison jumpsuits.

The judge in charge postponed the hearing until October 5 to allow defense lawyers to study the case files.

Abbas al-Maliki, a court-appointed solicitor for one of the prisoners, told Reuters that his client was facing allegations of ISIS membership.

In 2014, the terrorist group ISIS took control of large areas in Iraq and Syria before being defeated in 2017.

Over five million Iraqis had to flee the governorates of Nineveh, Salah al-Din, parts of Kirkuk, Diyala, and Anbar because of ISIS control over these areas in 2014.

Although Iraq declared in late 2017 that all of its regions were free of ISIS, the government continues to conduct security operations to hunt out any remaining members of the terrorist group.

Earlier this month, the Supreme Judicial Council of Iraq announced that it officially concluded the interrogation process for 5,704 ISIS detainees who were moved from northeastern Syria earlier this year, preparing them for trial.

The verified detainees originate from 67 different nationalities, including 3,497 Syrians and 474 Iraqis.

World.title: Iraq opens restricted air zones for civilian aviation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has lifted its decade-long military restrictions on western airspace, returning full control to civilian authorities.

The Iraqi Ministry of Transport announced on Friday that it has fully eliminated the restricted zones, thereby restoring complete sovereignty over the country’s airspace.

Iraq’s General Company for Air Navigation Services (GCANS) now controls all previously restricted military zones, which range from the northern province of Nineveh to the southern desert in Anbar province.

Between 2016 and 2017, the airspace was restricted to civilian planes. The Iraqi Air Force and the US-led international coalition used it only for combat missions against ISIS.

The decision would enable foreign airlines to use shorter and more efficient international flight corridors. The decision is expected to reduce operational rates for global airlines and simultaneously boost transit charge revenue for the Iraqi government.

The Transport Ministry in Iraq announced that the removal of these restrictions is part of the withdrawal process, as Iraq and the United States work together to coordinate the departure of the US-led international coalition’s remaining forces.

Technical and legal alignment for completely integrating the newly available routes into civilian flight is projected to be completed by October 1, 2026.

World.title: US dollar eases below 160,000 IQD across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The U.S. dollar experienced a slight retreat across parallel currency exchanges in Iraq on Sunday, September 20, 2026, dipping marginally below the 160,000-dinar mark recorded over the weekend while continuing to trade at a substantial premium above the official state benchmark.

According to market data, parallel bureaus across major trading hubs posted quotes well above the Central Bank of Iraq’s (CBI) official rate of 131,000 dinars per $100.

In the capital city of Baghdad, exchange bureaus quoted selling rates at 159,750 dinars per $100, with buying rates settling at 159,000 dinars.

Trading across northern financial desks in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan Region, reflected a slightly softer posture, posting selling prices of 158,700 dinars per $100 against buying levels of 158,250 dinars. In the southern economic hub of Basra, rates closely aligned with northern counters, recording 159,000 dinars for sale and 158,500 dinars for purchase.

While the day’s trades reflect a fractional cooling of roughly 250 to 950 dinars compared to Saturday’s peak surges, currency desks continue to price in significant liquidity risk.

The persistent spread between the parallel exchanges and the statutory peg highlights ongoing domestic cash-flow constraints and defensive trading behavior among market participants ahead of the critical September 30 deadline.

World.title: Washington Institute urges sanctions on Maliki and Ameri over disarmament delays
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A policy analysis published by the Washington Institute for Near East Policy has recommended that the United States prepare targeted individual sanctions against former Iraqi Prime Minister Nouri Al-Maliki and Badr Organization leader Hadi Al-Ameri if both figures continue obstructing federal efforts to disarm armed factions.

The study, authored by former U.S. Assistant Secretary of State David Schenker and reported by the 964 Network, argues that the two veteran political leaders—who collectively command 47 parliamentary seats within the ruling Coordination Framework—remain entrenched in maximalist positions rather than facilitating genuine state control over weapons, particularly following high-profile cross-border drone strikes against regional energy targets.

The analysis highlights that while Al-Maliki previously pledged to defuse factional tensions and avert collisions with Baghdad’s sovereign agenda, Iranian-backed groups within the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) subsequently launched an explosive drone barrage on September 10 targeting Saudi Arabia’s East-West crude pipeline near Yanbu, Riyadh, and Medina.

The assault, which temporarily disrupted up to 4–5 million barrels per day of transit to the Red Sea, directly undermined Coordination Framework claims of having neutralized escalation risks, exposing the fragility of domestic political assurances.

Schenker notes that Al-Maliki narrowly escaped U.S. Treasury designations during the first Trump administration and warns that continued efforts to replace disarmament with ambiguous “containment” models—akin to Lebanese political formulas surrounding Hezbollah—should trigger direct U.S. financial designations against both Al-Maliki and Al-Ameri.

The policy paper comes as Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi approaches his self-imposed September 30 deadline to monopolize arms under sovereign command—a date that coincides with the scheduled conclusion of the U.S.-led International Coalition’s mission in Iraq.

While moderate factions like Asa’ib Ahl al-Haq and Kata’ib Imam Ali offered preliminary disarmament concessions, and Muqtada Al-Sadr agreed to absorb Saraya Al-Salam into the regular military, hardline elements led by Kata’ib Hezbollah, Harakat Hezbollah Al-Nujaba, and Kata’ib Sayyid Al-Shuhada have openly resisted.

Bolstered by summer visits from IRGC Quds Force Commander Esmail Qaani, these groups have conditioned disarmament on non-starter demands, including dissolving the constitutionally recognized Kurdish Peshmerga, expelling Turkish forces, and enshrining PMF benefits by statute, while proposing unacceptable workarounds such as storing heavy weaponry in Iran or maintaining private depots under a nominal two-year activity freeze.

To reinforce Baghdad’s authority and protect vital regional energy corridors, the Washington Institute urges the White House to pursue calibrated pressure rather than sweeping economic embargoes, outlining several immediate policy steps:

World.title: Iraq’s University of Technology explores academic partnerships in Spain
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s University of Technology conducted high-level academic discussions on Saturday, September 19, 2026, with Spain’s University of Seville and University of Granada, aiming to broaden bilateral research cooperation, facilitate student and faculty exchanges, and launch joint scientific projects.

According to an official university statement carried by INA, the institutional visit was led by the President of the University of Technology, Mohsen Nouri Hamza, heading a senior academic delegation as part of the institution’s broader strategy to expand global academic engagement.

At the University of Granada, Hamza met with University Rector Pedro Mercado Pacheco to review frameworks for institutional collaboration and advance a draft comprehensive Global Agreement designed to govern future academic and scientific ties.

The delegation held additional technical sessions with Irene Pedreira Romero, Director of International Projects and Networks, and Leandro Di Stasi, Director of Internationalization at the International School for Postgraduate Studies.

Deliberations centered on establishing joint research initiatives and leveraging opportunities under the European Union’s Erasmus+ program to facilitate bilateral mobility for researchers, instructors, and graduate students, including hosting Iraqi postgraduate candidates in Spanish laboratories to carry out specialized thesis work.

The mission to the University of Seville focused on technical and engineering disciplines aligned with national development priorities. Talks concentrated on joint projects in renewable energy, industrial catalysts, advanced materials, structural engineering, and sustainable architectural design.

The Iraqi delegation—which included Dean of the College of Architecture Abbas Ali Hamza, Dean of the College of Electromechanical Engineering Ghassan Abdul Hussein Bilal, Materials Engineering faculty member Mohammed Al-Zuhairi, and Electromechanical Engineering faculty member Sundus Samir Jumaa—agreed to establish specialized bilateral research teams aimed at supporting sustainable development through academic innovation.

World.title: SIR assault on Constitution, says Congress
World.content:
Jairam Ramesh in a statement said, âWith this SIR, the State has abdicated its responsibility

NEW DELHI: Citing data to flag issues in the ongoing special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, Congress Sunday alleged the exercise was actually a massive "Shah instigated removal of voters" and an "assault on Constitution".Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh in a statement said, "With this SIR, the State has abdicated its responsibility and shifted the burden onto citizens to produce documents it may never have provided them. A test that the overwhelming majority of citizens cannot pass is just a machine for exclusion."Over the first two phases of SIR, names of 7.8 crore voters were deleted, he said. "The deletion rate as a proportion of the pre-SIR electoral roll is 13%," Ramesh said.

World.title: Bengal SIR tribunals may take 12 years to decide on appeals
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The innumerable voters in West Bengal who were removed from the electoral rolls after special intensive revision (SIR) may not be able to vote for more than a decade as appellate tribunals set up by Supreme Court could take more than 12 years to decide on their appeals for inclusion, going by the present pace of adjudication.

An affidavit filed by Election Commission before Supreme Court says 1,26,194 applications have been decided by tribunals in the last five months since they started functioning in mid-April. So, on average, 25,238 cases are being decided by the tribunals in a month when even Saturdays and Sundays are included as working days. The total number of pending cases as of Sept 16, when the affidavit was filed, was 37,05,235.

At current speed, if the tribunals work seven days a week, it would take 146 months to decide all cases.

Excessive backlog

Admitting that the present infrastructure and number of tribunals are insufficient to handle the Herculean task of adjudicating 37 lakh cases, the poll panel pleaded with the court to increase the number of tribunals in the state from 24 to 42, almost double the present strength, and allow judicial officers to work from home.





"With a view to further streamlining and expediting the disposal of the pending appeals, it is proposed that the number of appellate tribunals in the state of West Bengal may be considered for increase to correspond with the number of parliamentary constituencies in the state, so as to facilitate expeditious disposal of the pending appeals," said the affidavit, filed in response to a petition from TMC MP Derek O' Brien.

Allowing judicial workers to conduct hearings and undertake other proceedings from home "would assist in expediting the disposal of pending appeals by minimising the time lost in conveyance", it said.

In another affidavit filed in response to a petition on the functioning of the tribunals, the commission said they were constituted pursuant to the directives of the apex court and the standard operating procedure (SOP) governing their functioning has been formulated by the committee constituted for this purpose, comprising, inter alia, former judges of the high court at Calcutta.

World.title: Delhi high court gets 7 new judges
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The law ministry has notified the appointment of 14 new judges to four high courts, which include Delhi, Karnataka, Jharkhand, and J&K and Ladakh. The oath of office to the judges will be administered Monday.

The appointees were judicial officers who were earlier recommended by Supreme Court collegium to be elevated to the different HCs. There are still several recommendations of the collegium pending due to procedural issues.

Govt Saturday notified the appointment of seven judicial officers to be judges of Delhi HC. Those elevated include Nivedita Anil Sharma and Nisha Sahay Saxena, both made permanent judges of HC, and Sanjay Sharma, Bharat Parashar, Dinesh Bhatt, Arun Bhardwaj and Aditi Choudhary as additional judges, appointed for two years.

Usharani, Kuruba Shanthappa Bharath Kumar and Nerale Veerabhadraiah Bhavani have been appointed as additional judges of the Karnataka high court.

World.title: Using recovery agents proves costly for truck financier, SC orders Rs 15 lakh payout
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Criticising the use of muscle power by financiers to get back hypothecated vehicles,

has told one of them to pay Rs 15 lakh to a truck owner who had taken a loan of Rs 10.4 lakh to buy the vehicle.

Nearly two years after sanctioning the loan in June 2021, Cholamandalam Investment and Finance stealthily took back the truck over default in payment of EMIs. CCTV footage of a godown in Ayodhya on April 9, 2023, showed four persons breaking the vehicle's steering lock around 1am and driving it away. Six months later, Cholamandalam sent a notice saying it had taken back the vehicle and auctioned it for Rs 4.5 lakh, and the balance amount of Rs 1.3 lakh was still to be paid by him.

World.title: 93% of deleted Bengal voters have won appeals, EC tells SC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Around 93% of those whose cases have been decided so far over not being able to vote in the West Bengal polls this year because of doubts raised about their eligibility during Election Commission's SIR drive have won their appeals and have been included in the electoral roll.

However, 8,649 of 1.2 lakh lost their appeal and will be deleted.

The numbers, mentioned in an annexure to an affidavit filed by EC in Supreme Court, showed that 1,13,943 could satisfy the tribunals that the commission's decision to exclude them from the roll was incorrect, and this may intensify criticism of the poll panel.

Curiously, while the affidavit - filed to counter the claim of TMC and its MP, Derek O'Brien, that the exclusions cost them 31 assembly seats - puts the number of cases decided until Sept 16 at 1,26,194, the annexure stated that 1,22,592 were decided by the 24 tribunals until Sept 10.

EC sources, however, said the number of disposed of cases was too low to be seen as representative of the final outcome of all cases. They also said the results might favour inclusion because cases where citizens had documentary proof were decided first.

The annexure also mentioned district-wise filing of appeals by voters and disposal of cases. The appellate tribunals were set up on SC's direction that panels comprising former HC chief justices and judges would hear appeals against exclusions in the roll revision process.





A person whose claim for inclusion was rejected could approach the tribunals, which had started hearing appeals in April.

Claiming that O'Brien had misled the court, EC said, "It is pertinent to note that the applicant has conspicuously ignored the other side of the very same data relied upon by it. As disclosed in the applicant's own application, in as many as 21 constituencies, the number of deletions under adjudication exceeds the margin of victory of the candidates belonging to the applicant's own party."

The affidavit said that applying the very same test and reasoning propounded by the applicant, "the applicant would, therefore, equally have to seek setting aside of the election results in those constituencies won by its own party candidates".

"The selective and inconsistent application of an inherently flawed and speculative yardstick, therefore, exposes the self-serving and mala fide nature of the present application," it said.

EC said the attempt to portray all deletions as "effective disenfranchisement" was wholly incorrect and misleading. "It is humbly submitted that even assuming, without admitting, the correctness of the figures relied upon by the applicant, once the removals pertaining to ineligible ASDD (absent, shifted, duplicate/dead, and demoted/displaced) entries are excluded, the applicant's own data demonstrates that in several constituencies, the number of adjud-icated deletions is lower than the margin of defeat," it said.

This data, therefore, "completely demolished" the "speculative theory that the adjudication exercise altered the electoral outcome," the affidavit said.

Sikh bus driver attacked and thrown from vehicle in England; hijacked bus crashes into multiple cars before suspect is arrested.

LONDON: A 33-year-old Yemeni national was arrested for allegedly assaulting a British Sikh bus driver, vandalising the vehicle, hijacking it and crashing the bus into multiple vehicles in Telford, in Englandâs West Midlands region, last week.The unprovoked attack occurred around 6.37pm at Court Street in Madeley, Shropshire, on Sept 18. Video footage shared by a bystander showed the accused, Ali Balhad, grabbing the driver, punching him and tugging at his beard. The attacker was seen pulling out the cash register and hurling it at the driver.Throughout the ordeal, the driver appeared calm, holding on to his beard and begging people around to call the police. âJust take this guy away from me,â he was heard saying.To distract the attacker, Kymberlee Daley (19), who filmed the assault, told him that she had called the police, allowing the driver to jump out of the bus window and flee. To her horror, Balhad took the wheel and started driving the single-decker bus the wrong way down the street.The bus collided with multiple vehicles before coming to a stop, even as shocked bystanders chased it.Armed officers arrived at the scene within 10 minutes and arrested Balhad, who had been in Telford for about a week. The accused was remanded in custody and is due to appear before Telford Magistratesâ Court Monday.Paramedics treated the bus driver for minor injuries, West Mercia police said.

World.title: Punjab CM launches 'Mann Da Munafa' door-to-door campaign highlighting welfare initiatives
World.content:
Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann on Sunday launched the AAP's door-to-door election campaign for the 2027 Punjab assembly polls, pitching his government's 'Mann Da Munafa' narrative, claiming that every family is receiving an annual benefit of Rs 1.82 lakh from its welfare initiatives like free electricity and healthcare.

Mann said the AAP would go to every household with its record of work undertaken since 2022, while asserting that the campaign would remain positive and focus on what the government has delivered for Punjab.

He said the AAP would seek people's support based on the work delivered on the ground and question the opposition over its record and the issue of combating drugs.

During the outreach, Mann went door-to-door in Dhuri, met several families and interacted with elderly residents, women, youngsters and children.

He listened to their views, discussed the work undertaken by the government over the past four-and-a-half years and explained how various schemes and initiatives were translating into direct benefits for ordinary households.

"Every family in Punjab is today benefiting by Rs 1.82 lakh annually from the initiatives rolled out by our government. This is not an abstract figure. It represents money a household no longer has to take out of its own pocket for electricity, healthcare, education and other essential services," he said.





"I want every family to sit down and calculate for itself how much it is saving every month. That is the real meaning of 'Mann Da Munafa'," Mann added.

Claiming that his welfare initiatives reduced the financial burden of essential services on families, the chief minister said the government allowed them to use their hard-earned money for other household needs.

"Free electricity, healthcare, education, and Maavan Dheeyan Satkar Yojna are helping people save their hard-earned money.

Lakhs of households across Punjab are receiving zero electricity bills, which means that money that earlier went towards electricity charges can now be spent on children, homes and farms," he said.

"The expansion of primary healthcare has also meant that a fever, a check-up or a basic diagnostic test does not have to force a family to borrow money or dip into its savings," Mann added.

He said improvements in government schools have given parents greater confidence to educate their children without the burden of private fees.

"For decades, the people of Punjab paid taxes without receiving facilities in proportion to what they contributed. Our government is working to close that gap by directing resources towards households rather than privilege," the CM said.

"Mann Da Munafa is a simple question for every family: how much better off is your household today than it was before? Calculate what you save every month, and that answer will speak louder than any campaign speech," he said.

Speaking about rural development, Mann said his government changed how resources were allocated to villages and made village-level development a central part of its approach.

On the campaign strategy, he said AAP would keep its election campaign focused on its governance record rather than personal attacks or negativity.

"Our entire election campaign will remain positive. We will talk only about our work. We will place our record before the people and let them judge it, rather than build a campaign on abuse and negativity," he said.

"Our workers and candidates will carry the same message into every constituency: the savings delivered to families, the villages developed and public money spent on public welfare," he added.

He said the door-to-door outreach provided the most direct opportunity for political representatives to account for their work before the people, adding that the campaign would be taken across Punjab, with party workers and candidates presenting the government's record directly before households.

World.title: BJP, Congress trade barbs over PM Modi mimicry at Rahul Gandhi’s Indore event
World.content:
NEW DELHI: BJP on Sunday criticised the Congress after stand-up comedian Pulkit Mani mimicked Prime Minister Narendra Modi during an event attended by party leader Rahul Gandhi in Madhya Pradesh, with Union ministers and other BJP leaders targeting the opposition party and Congress MP over the performance.

The comedian performed the skit with the Rae Bareli MP during the latest edition of the âChhatron Ki Goonjâ event in Indore on Saturday. A video of the performance was shared by the Congress on X.

In the short act, Mani came on stage laughing and hugged Rahul. âMy friend. How are you?â he said. The Congress leader replied, âI'm fine; how are you, Modi ji?â Mani responded, âGreat harassmentâ, and continued laughing while repeatedly using the phrase âmy friendâ.

Rahul then said, âVery nice to meet you,â and asked Mani to âtell me moreâ. The comedian continued laughing and hugging Gandhi before saying, âMaa ko kursi do, maaâ, while pointing towards the audience.

BJP leaders hit out at Rahul Gandhi

Union minister Piyush Goyal reacted to the performance on X, calling Rahul âAsanskari naraz fufa (uncultured disgruntled uncle).â

âThe irony writes itself. The need to come on stage every now and then just to drag Prime Minister Modi ji's name into cheap political theatre never fails to amaze me,â Goyal said, asking the former Congress president to âlook in the mirrorâ.





Union minister Kiren Rijiju also criticised Rahul, saying, âI hadn't imagined that a party which was in power for nearly six decades would turn into such a circus that is busy entertaining their own shrunken supporters.â

Rijiju said Indians were proud that Prime Minister Modi was the âmost popularâ elected leader in the world.

âCongress party has become a party of comedians and Jokers! They are out forever.... RIP,â he said.

âDo you feel absolutely no shame in mocking an elderly mother and the Prime Minister of India?â Rijiju asked Rahul, while posting a video of PM Modi in which the prime minister is seen asking for a chair for an elderly woman who had attended one of his programmes.

BJP national general secretary Smriti Irani also reacted to the controversy, writing in Hindi on X, âJab nash manuj per chata hai, pehle vivek mar jaata haiâ (When doom looms over a person, it's his conscience that dies first).

BJP national secretary Sandeep Pathak called the mimicry act an expression of âdesperationâ and the âgrowing intellectual bankruptcyâ of the Congress.

âWhen you lose touch with India's values, you lose touch with India itself. And that is precisely where the Congress has lost its way,â Pathak, a Rajya Sabha MP, said on X.

Congress leaders defend programme

Congress leader Bhupesh Baghel hit back at the BJP's criticism, saying every person's mother deserved respect and questioning why similar concerns were not raised when the mothers of Rahul and other leaders were allegedly insulted.

âEveryone's mother is a mother, not PM Modi's mother alone. Why are their feelings not hurt when they insult Rahul Gandhi's mother or other leaders' mothers? This culture of insulting mothers was started by BJP-RSS and Mahamanav,â Baghel said.

Congress MP Imraan Masood said the âChhatron Ki Goonjâ programme had âshattered eardrumsâ of BJP leaders.

âLet the elections come. They will find out soon enough. 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' has shattered their eardrums.

They see Rahul Gandhi in their dreams and wake up with a start,â Masood said in Ranchi.

Congress leader TS Singh Deo said criticism and mimicry should not be objected to, but opposed the use of abusive language in public conversations.

âI do not think it is acceptable to stoop to the level of abusive language in a public conversation. But beyond that, if you're criticising someone in a normal way, even in a joking manner or with mimicry, no one should have any objection to it,â he said in Raipur.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

AICC general secretary Ghulam Ahmad Mir said the programme had received an overwhelming response and claimed that more than 200,000 young people had attended events under the initiative across India and Madhya Pradesh.

Rahul Gandhi had addressed students at the Indore session on issues including education costs and employment opportunities.

Congress leaders said the programme was focused on issues faced by young people and student welfare.

World.title: Asian Games 2026 LIVE | Mixed Doubles Group B: Tiwari-Meena vs Cambodia’s Viva-Chanroseka
World.content:
India’s premier soft tennis duo, Aadhya Tiwari and Jay Meena, are set to debut at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games with an early morning clash against Cambodia’s Viva Chao and Chanroseka Khun. Scheduled for 5:30 a.m. IST in Mixed Doubles Group B, the Indian pair—who already own a historic World Soft Tennis Championships bronze—will look to transition their extensive international training into an opening match on Monday (September 21, 2026).

Also Read | Continental glory: On the Asian Games 2026

Vidarsa K. Vinod has become the first woman from Keralam to win an Asian Games medal in shooting, securing silver in the women’s 10m air rifle team event at the 20th edition in Japan. This was Vinod’s first Asian Games, where she is also competing in the women’s 50m rifle 3 Positions event.

Also read: Asian Games | Shooting star Vidarsa aiming for higher accolades

World.title: ICE agent shoots, wounds man in Austin
World.content:
A U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer shot and wounded a man in Texas' capital of Austin, local authorities said, and anti-ICE protesters quickly gathered at the scene.

The unnamed man was in serious but stable condition at a hospital after being shot once in the torso on the city's north side Sunday afternoon (September 20, 2026), Austin Police Chief Lisa Davis said at a news conference with the mayor and other city officials.

The Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE, did not participate in the news conference and didn't immediately respond to requests for details.

Austin police officers were not involved in the operation or the shooting, which occurred after a traffic stop, Ms. Davis told reporters.

Austin Mayor Kirk Watson, a Democrat, said he wants the city's police department to be involved in the investigation so it can provide “clear, third-party eyes” in the process.

Mr. Watson said he does not think it would be appropriate for ICE to conduct an investigation on its own.

Austin residents have “a right to feel safe in their city,” Watson said. A proper investigation will only enhance credibility, he added.

Ms. Davis said she did not yet know the nationality of the person who was shot. The chief said there were not many facts she could provide so soon after the incident, but added that her department's special investigation unit was at the scene.

A dark blue Toyota Corolla was parked under an overpass with damage to its passenger-side door and what appeared to be bullet holes, local media reported.

A large law enforcement presence was at the scene, along with a crowd of about a hundred protesters. Some demonstrators cursed at police officers holding riot shields, while others yelled out as passing cars honked in support of the protest.

One man held a sign saying, “Nobody is safe” and, on the other side, “ICE Nazi.”

Asked if Austin authorities knew where the involved federal agent is, given that agents have left states after previous shootings nationwide, the mayor said: “We do not know that. But my hope would be that an agent that's involved in an officer-involved shooting would not leave the city. Certainly not leave the state."

U.S. Rep. Greg Casar, a Democrat representing parts of Austin, called for transparency as the shooting is investigated.

“It is awful that this horror has come to our doorstep," Mr. Casar told reporters. "For Austin to be safe, ICE should end its surge here.” The shooting comes as ICE surges enforcement across the country this summer, producing more than 50,000 arrests a month for the first time in its history in July and August.

In July, an ICE officer fatally shot 52-year-old Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, of Houston, after federal agents driving unmarked vehicles pursued him while he was taking his construction crew to a job site.

Also in July, 25-year-old Johan Sebastian, a Colombian man, was shot by an ICE officer in Maine. The officer is an Army veteran who has struggled with serious mental health issues since early childhood and never should have been given a badge and gun to patrol American streets, several of his close relatives told The Associated Press.

The administration's enforcement efforts were widely condemned last winter after the killings of Alex Pretti and Renee Good in Minnesota.

World.title: Australia completes cricket series sweep with 1-wicket win against Zimbabwe in third ODI
World.content:
Nathan Ellis made sure Josh Inglis' second ODI century didn't go to waste as Australia completed a 3-0 cricket series sweep against Zimbabwe with a thrilling one-wicket victory with one ball remaining on Sunday (September 20, 2026).

No. 9 batter Ellis made an unbeaten 36 off 44 balls in the third and final ODI to carry Australia to 272-9 in a successful chase that included Inglis' 103 off 102 but had looked like ending in failure.

“Great game of cricket,” Australia captain Mitchell Marsh said. “I thought Zimbabwe probably deserved to win, but the boys got the job done at the end there, and that was fantastic to see.” Zimbabwe, which earlier won the toss and scored 271-8 in its 50 overs, was heading for a consolation win when Inglis was clean bowled by skipper Sikandar Raza in the 42nd over. Australia still needed 45 more runs for victory.

Brad Evans (4-47 in 10 overs) reduced the tourists to 245-9 when he dismissed Adam Zampa in the 46th over.

But Ellis and Spencer Johnson (7 not out) shared an exciting last-wicket stand, which saw Wessly Madhevere drop Ellis in the penultimate over.

With nine needed off the final over, Madhevere got a chance to redeem himself, but Ellis smashed the spinner for a six off the first ball and then sealed the game by chipping the spinner over midwicket for the winning single off the fifth ball.

The one that got away

“I thought 280-290 was par with the bat, so to make a game out of 272 was a great effort,” Raza said. “As a captain, I'm really proud … I'd rather have a game like that than for the Aussies to just chase it down in 40 overs. A lot of positives, but it's the one that got away.” Australia beat the home team by 59 runs in the opening match and followed it up with an 84-run victory in the second game.

Evans put Australia in early trouble when he removed Marsh (8) and Travis Head (6) in his first two overs. Cooper Connolly (21) fell in the 13th over off a perfect leg break from Graeme Cremer — playing in his first ODI after eight years.

Inglis and Alex Carey (34) then dominated the spinners with their sweeps and reverse sweep shots in a 85-run stand and a scrappy Zimbabwe in the field.

Madhevere dropped Inglis at point before the batter completed his half-century. Evans broke the stand in his return spell when he dismissed Carey for the third time in the series, as Madhevere held onto a blinder at point to provide Zimbabwe with the much-needed breakthrough.

Australia's middle order got tangled up against Zimbabwe's spinners and slipped to 206-7 when Cremer had Xavier Bartlett lbw for 3. Inglis held one end up and raised his century off 94 balls with 11 fours before he tried to countercharge Raza.

Batters at ease

Raza earlier ensured Zimbabwe got its second-highest total batting against Australia in ODIs with an unbeaten 81. Innocent Kaia (55 retired hurt) and Craig Ervine (59) also scored valuable half centuries on a wicket where batters looked at ease in the day game.

Raza's decision to bat first for the first time in the series after winning the toss appeared to have paid off, and his team reached 148-2 in the 29th over before Kaia retired hurt with a hamstring injury.

Ervine and Raza set up Zimbabwe for a strong finish at 206-3 in 40 overs. But Australia allowed only 65 runs off the final 60 balls through some splendid bowling by Ellis, who took 3-50, and Johnson with 2-50.

World.title: Heavy rains, squally wind likely in West Bengal from September 22
World.content:
Parts of West Bengal are likely to receive heavy rainfall with gusty winds from September 22, 2026, due to a deep depression system forming over the Bay of Bengal.

According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), a low-pressure area over the east-central Bay of Bengal and adjoining north Andaman Sea is likely to intensify into a depression on Monday (September 21, 2026), bringing a spell of heavy rain and squally weather to West Bengal from September 22 to 26.

The intensity of rainfall in Bengal is likely to be higher in the coastal districts of Purba Medinipur and South 24 Parganas, with gusty winds reaching speeds of 40-50 kmph, it said.

Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds, reaching speeds of 30-40 kmph, are likely in one or two places in the remaining districts of south Bengal, including Kolkata, till September 25, the weather office said.

It said heavy rainfall will also occur in the sub-Himalayan districts of Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Jalpaiguri, Alipurduar and Cooch Behar from September 23 to 25.

Thunderstorms with gusty winds are likely over the other north Bengal districts of Uttar and Dakshin Dinajpur as well as Malda during the period, the IMD added.

"Continuing to move west-northwestwards, it is very likely to reach the west-central and adjoining northwest Bay of Bengal near the north Andhra Pradesh — South Odisha coasts around the morning of 23rd September. Southwest monsoon moderate to strong over Andaman Sea; moderate over Northeast, Eastcentral, Southeast Bay of Bengal; weak to moderate over Northwest, Westcentral, Southwest Bay of Bengal," said IMD.

IMD also advised the fishermen not to venture into the deep sea from 21st September along and off West Bengal coast and from 22nd September to 25th September. Fishermen are advised to return to the coast by the night of 21st September.

"Swell waves in the range of 16.0 - 19.0 sec period with 0.9 - 1.1 m height are forecast up to 20:30 hours on 21-09-2026. It was advised that there is a possibility of surging waves; boats to ply with utmost vigilance; recreation with due care," said IMD in its statement.

World.title: Asian Games 2026: Elavenil Valarivan fires India to twin silver delight on day one
World.content:
India’s shooting campaign at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games began on a high note, with experienced rifle shooter Elavenil Valarivan playing a starring role in the country’s double-silver haul in the women’s 10m air rifle competition, in Japan on Sunday (September 20, 2026).

Elavenil, one of India’s most accomplished rifle shooters, helped the country secure silver in the team event before adding an individual silver later in the day. The latter, however, came with a hint of disappointment as the Tamil Nadu-born shooter appeared firmly on course for gold for most of the final, only to see her challenge fade in the closing stages as Japan’s Hinata Taichi held her nerve to emerge champion.

The 2025 World Championship bronze medallist finished with 252.4 points, just 0.6 behind Taichi, who clinched gold with an Asian Games record 253.0.

South Korea’s Ban Hyo-jin, the reigning world champion and Paris Olympics gold medallist, took bronze with 230.4.

For Elavenil, the silver was her first individual medal at the Asian Games, having competed at the 2018 Jakarta and 2022 Hangzhou editions without making the podium.

She had looked in complete command for much of the final and seemed to have the gold within her sights. After the 17th shot, she held a 1.4-point advantage over Ban, with Taichi lying third. Even after the 21st shot, Elavenil was still ahead of the Japanese shooter by 0.2.

But as the pressure intensified, the margins narrowed.

Elavenil entered the final two shots just 0.3 points behind Taichi. She responded with a 10.4, but the Japanese shooter produced a 10.6 to stretch her advantage to 0.5.

With one shot remaining, Elavenil needed something special to turn the contest around. She managed 10.1. Taichi, however, held her nerve and answered with a 10.2 to secure gold and rewrite the Asian Games record.

Elavenil admitted that being in a commanding position may have allowed her concentration to dip slightly.

“I think I knew that somewhere I was in the top three and although I was coming back to focusing on my process and my technique, I did get a bit relaxed. I really need to work on my finals some more. I think that’s all. I felt I gave my absolute best and I’m glad it turned out that way,” she said.

The result capped a strong run for the Tamil Nadu-born shooter, who has been among India’s most consistent rifle exponents over the past year. She won silver at the 2025 Asian Championships in Shymkent and repeated that feat at the 2026 edition in New Delhi.

Before stepping onto the individual final range, however, Elavenil had already helped India open its shooting campaign with a silver medal in the women’s 10m air rifle team event.

Alongside Sonam Uttam Maskar and Asian Games debutant Vidarsa Vinod, she combined to give India its first medal from the shooting ranges.

The Indian trio aggregated 1898.0 points to finish second behind a dominant Chinese team, which shattered the qualification world record with 1904.2. China bettered its own previous mark of 1902.0, set at the Asian Championships in Shymkent last August.

The battle for the second step on the podium was far tighter. Japan finished third with 1897.1, just 0.9 points behind India, with the Indian trio holding its nerve when it mattered.

Team medals are decided on the basis of the three shooters’ qualification scores, making every shot significant.

Sonam, who finished third in qualification, led the Indian effort with an impressive 634.1. Elavenil added 633.5 to finish seventh, while Vidarsa shot 630.4 for 12th place.

Though Vidarsa missed the individual final, her contribution proved decisive in India’s silver-medal finish.

“Yes, it’s a great achievement. It’s another thing that I could not qualify for the final, but the team silver has given us a good start,” Vidarsa said.

The 27-year-old from Kerala also showed impressive composure on her Asian Games debut, refusing to be overwhelmed by the occasion.

“I was not nervous. I was confident and just focused on my shooting,” she said.

Her performance was particularly noteworthy because she had taken up the 10m air rifle event only two months ago. Her principal discipline is the 50m rifle 3-positions event, but she adapted quickly enough to produce a score that helped India stay ahead of Japan in a tense team battle.

“I am definitely confident that I will do much better in 50m 3-positions as it is my main event,” Vidarsa said.

China’s depth, meanwhile, was evident throughout qualification. Junior world champion Wang Zifei topped the standings with a stunning 638.8, setting a new qualification Asian record. Her compatriot Han Jiyan also made the individual final after scoring 633.8 to finish fifth.

China had three shooters inside the qualification positions, but with only two athletes from each country allowed to compete in the individual medal round, its third shooter missed out.

For India, the twin silvers offered an encouraging start to a shooting campaign carrying considerable expectations after the country’s record haul of 22 medals — seven gold, nine silver and six bronze — at the Hangzhou Asian Games.

World.title: Far-left Elif Eralp wins Berlin vote on anti-AfD, pro-poor campaign
World.content:
The far-left Die Linke party won Berlin elections Sunday (September 20, 2026), according to exit polls, making its lead candidate Elif Eralp the top contender to become the next mayor of Germany's capital city.

Ms. Eralp, 45, and her pro-poor party have promised dramatic steps to solve Berlin's housing crisis and bring down rents, including with a controversial pledge to expropriate flats held by large corporate landlords.

The daughter of Turkish migrants, Eralp has also campaigned as being the best person to counter the rise of the far-right and anti-immigration Alternative for Germany (AfD) party.

"I believe it would indeed send a powerful signal if someone with a migration background were to become governing mayor of Berlin," she said on the eve of the vote.

Celebrating on Sunday (September 20), she exclaimed: "In our city, love and justice have triumphed over hatred."

Ms. Eralp — whose party wants to reduce social inequality and the power of big business — has been compared to Zohran Mamdani, the charismatic left-wing outsider who became mayor of New York.

"Naturally, the success of a democratic socialist in New York — the heartland of capitalism — is a major success," Ms. Eralp said on Friday (September 18), calling Mr. Mamdani "a great role model".

The election win by the Die Linke, at about 25% according to exit polls, was a historic first for Berlin and dealt a blow to the centre-right CDU of embattled Chancellor Friedrich Merz, which came second with about 20%.

In order to govern, however, Eralp must now convince other parties — likely the centre-left SPD and the Greens — to join her in a so-called "red-red-green coalition".

West Asia conflict

However, the SPD's lead candidate Steffen Krach has already made clear he opposes the expropriation idea by Die Linke, a party which traces its roots in part to communist East Germany's ruling party.

Germany's mainstream parties have many other differences with the hard-left party, especially on security policy, where it opposes military aid for Ukraine and advocates for Germany to leave NATO.

Die Linke has also been criticised for anti-Israeli messages from some district-level figures — an especially sensitive issue in Germany, given its dark history of Nazi rule and the Holocaust.

Ms. Eralp had repeatedly emphasised her desire to support and foster Jewish life in Berlin.

But fierce criticism of Israel from some local branches of Die Linke, particularly in Berlin's Neukoelln neighbourhood that is home to many Arab and Muslim immigrants, have drawn negative headlines.

A concert in August at a local Die Linke campaign event in Neukoelln provoked scandal after a performer advocated an "intifada" (uprising) and chanted "Death to the IDF!", the Israel Defense Forces.

Ms. Eralp distanced herself from the incident, but it drew fierce criticism from the Greens and the SPD — and once again prompted the press to question whether Die Linke is fit for governing.

Path to power

Still, the Greens during the campaign appeared to prefer backing a coalition with Die Linke over the other obvious possibility of joining with the conservative CDU.

But in the SPD, which has a history of close ties to organised labour and working-class voters, there are some dissenting voices.

The SPD chose to break with a left-wing coalition after the previous election in 2023 and is currently junior partners with the CDU.

Ms. Eralp now has a few days or weeks to convince her potential partners that she has her state branch under control and is suited to govern.

Ms. Erlap's parents, who were active in socialist politics and trade unions in Turkey, fled to Germany in 1980 following a military coup when the mother was eight months pregnant.

Ms. Eralp was born in Munich and went on to study law in Hamburg, going on to defend migrants' rights. She was hired as a staffer for Die Linke's faction in the German parliament in 2010, and moved to Berlin permanently not long after.

She lives in the trendy Kreuzberg district with her husband and two children — and is often quick to emphasise that, like most Berliners, they rent their flat and are not homeowners.

World.title: Premier League: Man City outgun Sunderland despite Brobbey hat-trick, Liverpool marks Iraola’s winning return
World.content:
Manchester City went top of the Premier League despite Brian Brobbey's hat-trick in a 5-3 thriller on Sunday (September 20, 2026) as Matheus Cunha rescued Manchester United from another damaging defeat at Fulham.

City took advantage of Arsenal's shock 3-0 defeat at Brighton on Saturday (September 19) but made life hard for themselves despite taking the lead three times at the Etihad Stadium.

Enzo Fernandez opened the scoring with his first goal since equalling the Premier League transfer record with a £125 million ($167 million) move from Chelsea.

The Argentine midfielder's free-kick caught out Robin Roefs at his near post.

Sunderland won their first European match for 53 years against AZ Alkmaar in midweek but showed little sign of tiredness as City could not shake off the Black Cats.

Brobbey slotted home Enzo Le Fee's pass for the first of his treble.

Quick feet and a slick finish from Rayan Cherki restored City's advantage, but Brobbey again replied within four minutes at the end of a fine Sunderland move.

Antoine Semenyo smashed City back in front before half-time and thought he had settled the game with another accurate left-footed finish just before the hour mark.

Brobbey completed his hat-trick after Nilson Angulo beat Gianluigi Donnarumma to a ball over the top.

A couple of nervy moments from the Italian goalkeeper nearly led to a Sunderland equaliser as Ruben Dias was forced to clear off his own line.

However, Erling Haaland finally got involved in the goalfest to seal the three points and ensured he has scored against every side he has faced in the Premier League.

Victory extends Enzo Maresca's perfect start to the daunting task of succeeding Pep Guardiola at City boss.

"To be honest, I prefer to win 1-0 than 5-3 but I expected a very difficult game," said Maresca.

United fails to ease pressure on Carrick

United head into a three-week international break just two points outside the relegation zone as they failed to ease the pressure on manager Michael Carrick in a 1-1 draw.

But it could have been even worse for the Red Devils after a calamitous Lisandro Martinez own goal put Fulham on course for their first league win of the season.

Senne Lammens parried Calvin Bassey's strike back into the danger area and then could not clear when Martinez inadvertently turned the ball towards his own goal.

Cunha's 89th minute equaliser also took a wicked deflection off David Affengruber to save United's blushes.

The Red Devils have taken just five points from their opening five games and were dumped out of the League Cup by Brighton in midweek after surrendering a 2-0 lead at home for the first time in 50 years.

"We came to get the win of course, the way it panned out and the way we finished is the positive we take from it," said Carrick.

"We don't think things are perfect by any means. We need to win football matches."

A point is enough to edge Fulham off the foot of the table as Tottenham drop to the bottom.

Iraola's winning return

Liverpool won 1-0 on Andoni Iraola's return to Bournemouth thanks to Alexander Isak's winner.

Iraola was given a warm reception after leading the Cherries into Europe for the first time in the club's history.

That success led to the Basque being snapped up by Liverpool but he has endured an up and down start at Anfield and needed a victory to ease tensions before the international break.

Liverpool's performance was again far from convincing, but they got the only goal when Cody Gakpo's cross sat up for Isak to fire in his fourth of the season.

"To win here is very difficult, I know it very well," said Iraola. "Overall we've improved, definitely since the first games."

Victory moves Liverpool up to sixth and within a point of third-placed Brighton.

Leeds missed the chance to go third themselves after being held 0-0 at home by Crystal Palace.

World.title: INLD’s Sampat Singh attacks BJP’s ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyaan’, alleges misuse of State machinery
World.content:
Indian National Lok Dal patron and former minister Sampat Singh on Sunday (September 20, 2026) condemned the month-long “Seva Sankalp Abhiyaan” by the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party as an institutionalised campaign of self-glorification executed at the direct expense of the public exchequer, State machinery, and the dignity of the citizens.

Holding a press conference in Gurugram, Mr. Singh noted that the political landscape of contemporary India is increasingly witnessing the alarming substitution of substantive governance with theatrical pageantry, culminating in spectacles that openly mock democratic norms. A glaring manifestation of this “disturbing trend” unfolded right now during the ongoing rollout of these month-long celebrations, he said, adding that a critical examination of how this campaign was operationalised revealed a chilling mobilisation of the State apparatus.

Across multiple States and districts, administrative machinery — district collectors and police departments down to municipal bodies and government departments — was actively diverted from primary constitutional duties to orchestrate a centralised personality cult.

Official circulars issued to schools mandate that teachers and children organise massive deepotsav (festival of light) programmes, compelling classrooms to burn hundreds of lamps under administrative duress. This forced participation was not merely an administrative inconvenience; it represented a deep moral and financial corruption, said Mr. Singh. Public funds — derived from the hard-earned tax contributions of ordinary citizens — were squandered on multi-city rallies, massive cutouts and multi-crore media blitzes.

This hypocrisy, he said, became even more glaring when contrasted against the government’s own stated policies. On one hand, the Prime Minister issued clarion calls urging citizens to conserve resources and reduce oil consumption by 10% in the name of national interest; on the other, this massive, State-sponsored lamp-burning spree consumed precious oil on an industrial scale — resources that could be better utilised to alleviate the crippling cost-of-living crisis squeezing ordinary households.

He said this institutionalised hypocrisy unfolded against a backdrop of severe economic distress and skyrocketing prices during this month. Compounding this, the Indian Government has instituted a regressive 0.4% tax on UPI transactions above ₹2,000, buckling under pressure from the United States, he alleged, adding that looming geopolitical challenges like the ongoing Hormuz and Red Sea crises threatened to severely disrupt supply chains and accentuate economic difficulties for India.

World.title: Two officers among 6 martyred, 8 terrorists killed in Hangu fire exchange: ISPR
World.content:
Two officers and four others were martyred while eight terrorists were killed in a fire exchange in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Hangu district on Sunday, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said.

During an intense fire exchange between a “security forces convoy and Khwarij”, 23-year-old Captain Abuzar Farooq from Gujranwala and 22-year-old Lieutenant Sheraz Babar of Chakwal, “who were leading their troops from the front, fought gallantly and paid the ultimate sacrifice and embraced martyrdom along with their four men”.

According to images released by ISPR, the other four men comprised three sepoys and a “non-combatant”.

On the other hand, “eight Khwarij belonging to Indian-sponsored Fitna al Khwarij were sent to hell due to effective engagement by own troops”, the ISPR statement added.

The state uses the term Fitna al Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).

A sanitisation operation was being conducted to eliminate any other terrorist found in the area, ISPR said.

It affirmed that the “relentless counterterrorism campaign under vision ‘Azm-i- Istehkam’ (as approved by Federal Apex Committee on National Action Plan) by security forces and law enforcement agencies of Pakistan will continue at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country”.

“These sacrifices of our brave soldiers further reinforce our unwavering commitment to safeguarding our nation at all costs,” the military’s media wing stated.

Sunday’s development comes two days after a two-pronged assault near a mosque in the old Police Lines of KP’s Kohat district claimed 23 lives, including those of 17 policemen. Eight terrorists were killed during an overnight clearance operation launched to clear the area.

KP witnessed an increase in terrorist attacks in August compared with July, according to monthly data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS).

On August 7, a captain was martyred while seven terrorists were killed during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Hangu.

On July 30, a deputy superintendent of police (DSP) was among nine cops martyred and 28 others were injured after terrorists attacked the Khazina Banda checkpost in Hangu. Days later, security forces were reported to have killed the mastermind behind the attack.

World.title: Aleema detained under MPO in Lahore ahead of PTI's Sept 27 protest
World.content:
PTI said on Sunday that ex-prime minister and party founder Imran Khan’s sister, Aleema Khan, had been detained by authorities, after the office of Lahore’s deputy commissioner (DC) ordered her detention or arrest for 30 days.

The development takes place amid reports of a crackdown on the PTI ahead of its September 27 countrywide protest and march to Islamabad, which the party has called to demand Imran’s release from jail and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution.

The September 20 order, a copy of which is available with Dawn, said DC Muhammad Ali Ijaz had ordered the detention or arrest of Aleema and a man named Muhammad Ameer under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960 (MPO).

The MPO ordinance allows the authorities to order detention and restrict judicial review of such orders.
